papers.title: A Second-Order Cone Programming Approach to Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of Optimal Active and Reactive Power Dispatch for Microgrid System
papers.abstract: This paper aims to enhance Energy Management System (EMS) in a microgrid by integrating Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) with Optimal Active and Reactive Power Dispatch in accordance with Optimal Power Flow techniques. In power system architecture, we consider the setting of tap-changing transformers and reactive power compensators as additional decision variables in the microgrid. This approach enables efficient and reliable system operation by minimizing Total Power Loss in transmission lines while considering Total Operating Cost (TOC) and Total Carbon Dioxide Emissions (TCOE). We then formulate the multi-objective function by combining these three objective functions and name the new function Combined Economic, Emission, and Power Loss. The proposed work leverages NMPC to optimize power dispatch from various energy sources within the microgrid on a time-varying basis. The NMPC problem can be cast as a Second-Order Cone Program. This proposed formulation proves that reactive power dispatch can be applied successfully with real power dispatch in the NMPC for better energy management in a microgrid. It reduces power loss in transmission lines and improves overall energy efficiency. Additionally, because of lower power loss, it leads to a decrease in both TOC and TCOE compared to the previous EMS without reactive power dispatch. Moreover, the proposed approach transforms the nonconvex problem into the convex SOCP which can be solved with an efficient solver, such as the interior-point method, and global optimality can be guaranteed. To prove the theoretical result, the proposed EMS is validated through simulations on the Mae Hong Son microgrid.

papers.title: EEG-Based ADHD Detection Framework Using Local Pattern Descriptors and Bayesian-Optimized Machine Learning Classifiers
papers.abstract: Although clinical diagnosis of childhood Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) relies heavily on subjective behavioral assessments, electroencephalography (EEG) offers a low-cost, noninvasive objective alternative. This study proposes an approach employing 1D texture analysis of EEG signals for ADHD classification. Specifically, 1D Local Binary Pattern (1D-LBP), 1D Local Gradient Pattern (1D-LGP), and 1D Local Neighbor Descriptive Pattern (1D-LNDP) capture local amplitude relationships across 19 electrodes in 2-second frames, yielding a combined 570-dimensional feature space based on binary transitions. To optimize this, the minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) method is used to select the 190 most discriminative features (Hybrid-190). System performance was then evaluated using various classifiers, with hyperparameters tuned via Bayesian optimization within a 5-fold cross-validation scheme. Tested on a benchmark dataset of 61 children with ADHD and 60 healthy controls, the framework achieved a peak segment-level accuracy of 99.63%, a specificity of 99.65%, an F1-score of 99.67%, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9987 using a k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classifier. Under a subject-independent protocol with per-participant aggregation, it attained a participant-level accuracy of 78.50% and an AUC of 0.8600 with a Random Forest classifier. A topographic accuracy peak was also observed in the right temporal-occipital region near the T6 electrode. Among individual descriptors, 1D-LGP achieved the highest standalone segment-level accuracy at 99.26%. Ultimately, this framework provides an interpretable and computationally efficient EEG-based approach whose subject-independent performance supports its potential for clinical decision-support systems.

papers.title: ATFM Delay Prediction With an Enhanced Index System: A Bayesian-Optimized XGBoost Model Incorporating Airway Network Characteristics
papers.abstract: Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) delay quantitatively represents the spatiotemporal distribution of congestion arising from imbalances between capacity and demand within the airspace network. To enhance prediction accuracy, this study develops an enhanced index system that integrates airway-related factors encompassing structural and operational characteristics, together with critical delay determinants such as waypoint degree, average shortest path length, and congestion propagation rate. The proposed framework utilizes a Bayesian-optimized XGBoost (BO-XGBoost) model, wherein a Gaussian Process-guided search is implemented to identify an optimal hyperparameter configuration(nest=269 ,dmax=7) that balances model complexity with generalization. Comparative benchmarking reveals that BO-XGBoost attains an accuracy of 81.0% and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.88, significantly outperforming Random Forest (AUC=0.85) and LSTM (AUC=0.84) baselines while exhibiting superior computational efficiency. Controlled ablation studies further substantiate the efficacy of the proposed index system. Compared to a baseline metric system excluding airway factors, the integrated approach yields improvements of 4% in accuracy, 9% in recall, and 4% in AUC. Relative to a system incorporating airway factors alone, the proposed model demonstrates gains of 7% in accuracy, 23% in recall, and 11% in AUC. Finally, SHAP-based interpretability analysis identifies airway flow dynamics and topological metrics as dominant predictors. These results underscore the reliability of the enhanced index system as a robust foundation for proactive ATFM decision-making in complex airspace environments.

papers.title: Design of Occupancy-Based Supervisory Model Predictive Control for HVAC Systems in Office Buildings Considering Energy Efficiency and Thermal Comfort
papers.abstract: Globally, electricity demand has increased due to climate change and population growth, leading to higher energy consumption in building Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems. Traditional HVAC control methods using static setpoints and manual on/off often waste energy and fail to maintain occupant comfort because of their limited responsiveness to changes in occupancy and weather conditions. This paper proposes a hierarchical occupancy-based supervisory model predictive control (SMPC) framework for HVAC systems, leveraging machine learning for empirical model identification. Based on real measurements, a dynamic model of building zone and HVAC system is developed, integrating temperature and humidity control while capturing the interactions between occupancy thermal loads, HVAC states, and environmental conditions. The control design consists of a supervisory control (SC) layer and a model predictive control (MPC) layer. The SC layer formulates an optimal setpoint design that minimizes the weighted sum of total operating cost (TOC) and thermal comfort cost (TCC). Thermal comfort is quantified using the Predicted Mean Vote (PMV), based on which a novel method is formulated to derive temperature setpoint bounds that directly relate the control formulation to occupant thermal comfort. The MPC layer tracks the optimal set-point generated by the SC layer using a cost function that penalizes both tracking errors and excessive actuator usage. The proposed controller is implemented on a single-zone HVAC system, where HVAC electrical power and moisture removal rate are treated as control inputs, while weather conditions and occupancy-driven thermal loads are incorporated as forecasted disturbances. Numerical results demonstrate excellent performance in reference tracking, with significant reductions in peak load and TOC compared to nominal operation, while thermal comfort is maintained within acceptable limits.

papers.title: From Visualization Concepts to Physical Games: Engaging Students Through Active Learning
papers.abstract: The competency-based learning approach challenges professors to rethink the learning process. Elements of human behavior, such as collaboration, inventiveness, proactivity, and self-direction, should be developed by students. As these elements are not taught explicitly, professors are encouraged to use active learning methods to support their development; the same applies to data visualization education. In this context, we present an off-screen classroom experience that uses a learning method to design and use non-digital games in a Data Visualization course. This activity was applied through four Data Visualization classes from 2024 to 2025. Student evaluations indicate that it supports self-assessment of learning, reinforces conceptual understanding, and promotes high levels of engagement and enjoyment during the learning process.

papers.title: Enhanced Seismic Response Prediction of Multivariate Rocking Bridges using Active Learning
papers.abstract: Objective Self-centering rocking bridges can reduce residual displacement and structural damage after earthquakes, but their seismic responses are strongly affected by interface opening and closing, impact interaction, energy dissipation, and coupled uncertainties from structural parameters and ground motions. Nonlinear time history analysis (NLTHA) based on high-fidelity finite element models is commonly used to evaluate such responses, but repeated simulations under large-scale random samples are computationally expensive. Conventional passive sampling methods may also waste computational resources on redundant samples and may not efficiently capture highly nonlinear response regions. To address this problem, an active-learning-enhanced surrogate modeling framework was developed for efficient seismic response prediction of multivariate rocking bridges. The objective was to reduce the number of NLTHA samples while maintaining prediction accuracy close to that of a full-data regression model.Methods A four-span continuous concrete box-girder bridge with prestressed rocking piers was selected as the benchmark structure, and a three-dimensional finite element model was established in OpenSees. Reinforced concrete piers were modeled using fiber-section nonlinear beam-column elements; concrete and reinforcing steel were simulated with nonlinear material models; prestressing tendons were modeled using truss elements with initial strain to represent the initial prestress; and energy-dissipation rebars were arranged around the rocking interface. The rocking interface was represented by vertical zero-length compression-only contact elements. The circular interface was divided into circumferential sectors and radial rings, forming wedge-shaped contact subregions to reproduce the compression behavior during interface opening and closing. The abutment, shear key, pounding interaction, backfill soil, pile foundation, and sliding bearing were also represented using nonlinear constitutive relationships. The rocking pier model was validated by comparison with quasi-static test results, and the simulated hysteretic responses were generally consistent with the experimental force–displacement curves. To consider multi-source uncertainties, 11 structural parameters and 6 ground motion intensity measures (IMs) were used as candidate input variables. A total of 1000 bridge samples were generated by Latin hypercube sampling, and 1000 ground motion records were constructed by selection and scaling. Each bridge model was randomly paired with one ground motion record, and NLTHA was conducted to obtain engineering demand parameters (EDPs), including peak drift ratio of the pier, residual drift ratio of the pier, bearing displacement, and abutment displacement. After removing non-convergent analyses and statistical outliers identified by the interquartile range method, 968 valid input–output data pairs were obtained. The dataset was standardized and divided into training and testing subsets at a ratio of 8:2. Natural Gradient Boosting (NGB) was adopted as the surrogate model because it provides both predicted mean values and predictive distributions, allowing uncertainty estimation during active learning. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and five-fold cross-validation were used to tune the model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to quantify the contribution of input variables to different EDP predictions. Based on feature importance results, 11 structural parameters and the three most important IMs were retained as model inputs. Four sampling strategies were compared: random sampling (RS), Query-by-Committee (QBC), Greedy Sampling in Input Space (GSx), and Greedy Sampling in Output Space (GSy). The active learning process started from a small labeled set, then iteratively selected informative unlabeled samples for additional NLTHA and model retraining. The convergence and prediction accuracy were evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R²), mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE). The effects of batch size and committee size on QBC performance were further investigated.Results and Discussions The SHAP analysis showed that IMs contributed more significantly to displacement response prediction than most structural parameters. Among the candidate IMs, the spectral displacement at the fundamental period, Sd-T1, had the highest average importance for pier, bearing, and abutment displacement responses. This indicates that a displacement-related and structure-dependent IM can better reflect the deformation demand of rocking bridges. Among structural parameters, pier diameter, pier height, and damping ratio had relatively large effects on pier drift responses. The energy dissipation rebar ratio contributed more to peak drift than to residual drift, suggesting that different structural parameters affect peak and residual responses in different ways. The comparison of sampling strategies showed that active learning generally outperformed RS under the same number of queried samples. RS exhibited slower convergence because samples were selected without considering model uncertainty or response-space information. QBC showed the best overall performance. When the number of queried samples reached approximately 60, the R² of QBC approached or exceeded 0.8, while MAE and RMSE decreased rapidly and became stable. GSx and GSy also improved the model accuracy compared with RS, but they required more samples to reach a similar error level. The better performance of QBC was mainly attributed to its use of model uncertainty, which enabled the learning process to focus on samples with higher information gain. The parameter analysis of QBC indicated that batch size and committee size affected convergence efficiency and prediction stability. For batch sizes of 1, 5, and 10, the prediction performance became close when the queried sample number increased, but a moderate batch size provided a better balance between model updating frequency and computational cost. For committee sizes of 1, 5, and 10, a committee size of 5 produced better overall R², MAE, and RMSE in the middle and later stages of active learning. Therefore, a batch size of 5 and a committee size of 5 were selected as the final QBC settings. The active learning model was further compared with the full-data regression model. The full-data model used 774 training samples, whereas the active learning model used only 77 samples selected by QBC, corresponding to about 10% of the training set. Although the active learning model produced slightly larger errors, the overall error increase remained within 18%. The largest increase appeared in abutment displacement prediction, where RMSE increased from 0.316 to 0.373, corresponding to an error increase of 17.72%. This was mainly related to the stronger nonlinearity caused by soil–structure interaction and pounding effects, as well as the limited coverage of large-displacement and impact-response samples. For bearing displacement, the increases in RMSE and MAE were 14.69% and 14.29%, respectively. These results indicate that the active learning framework can substantially reduce the demand for labeled NLTHA samples while maintaining prediction accuracy close to that of full-data training.Conclusions An active-learning-enhanced NGB surrogate model was developed for seismic response prediction of multivariate prestressed rocking bridges. The results indicate that Sd-T1 is the most influential IM for displacement response prediction, and QBC is more efficient than GSx, GSy, and RS in terms of convergence speed and prediction accuracy. With optimized parameters, the QBC-based active learning model required only about 10% of the training samples and limited the overall error increase to less than 18% compared with the full-data model. The proposed framework provides an efficient approach for reducing NLTHA costs in seismic demand prediction of rocking bridges. Future work should further examine the coverage of boundary and extreme response regions, include experimental calibration, and extend the framework to bridge systems with nonuniform pier parameters.

papers.title: Compact, Low-Profile, Dual-Polarized Metasurface Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth Using MLP-Assisted Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: A compact, low-profile, dual-polarized metasurface (MS) antenna with enhanced bandwidth, empowered by machine learning optimization, is presented. Unlike slot-coupled MS antennas, which suffer from non-negligible backward radiation, and dipole-induced MS antennas, which suffer from a high profile, the developed antenna features a low-profile configuration while being backed by a complete ground plane. The antenna adopts a novel ring-induced 2×2 MS radiator, which effectively produces two well-merged resonances under a low-profile configuration. To efficiently explore the high-dimensional design space and achieve the widest bandwidth possible, a joint optimization framework integrating a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with Bayesian optimization (BO) is developed. Measured results demonstrate that the optimized antenna, occupying a compact footprint of 0.44λ0 × 0.44λ0 × 0.035λ0, achieves a broad bandwidth of 21.3% while maintaining port isolation exceeding 25 dB and stable broadside radiation performance.

papers.title: Mitigating Knowledge Decay in Engineering Calculus Through Spaced Repetition and Active Learning
papers.abstract: The teaching of Differential and Integral Calculus in engineering programs faces historically high failure rates, frequently associated with ineffective study habits such as massed practice. This article investigates the impact of the application of spacing in an educational context, integrated with active learning methodologies, on academic performance and knowledge retention. Through a quasi-experimental study with 113 Electrical and Computer Engineering students, a control group following standard blended learning with autonomous study time management was compared to an experimental group subjected to a rigorous protocol of scheduled spaced reviews, including a critical intervention conducted 48 hours after the initial lecture. The results demonstrated that the experimental group achieved an 86.60% rise in the pass rate compared to the control group. Furthermore, a shift in grades to higher ranges was observed, raising the median to 5.0 and allowing the average student to move from direct failure to being eligible for the Remedial Exam. Despite the increase in grade dispersion, a higher concentration of students was observed in performance ranges compatible with passing the course. Taken together, the findings suggest that the intervention in the temporal structuring of study, conducted 48 hours after the initial lecture and focused on addressing the forgetting curve, constitutes a low-cost and scalable strategy for reducing immediate failure in advanced courses, such as Differential and Integral Calculus II for Engineering.

papers.title: Gamification and active learning in project management: A replicable model for business and management education
papers.abstract: In Engineering education, a gamification-based pedagogical tool has been introduced to enhance the teaching of project management. This innovative approach aims to equip students with essential skills to tackle contemporary engineering challenges. Recognizing the importance of project management in engineering, the study focuses on the Scrum framework, known for promoting collaboration and adaptability. It hypothesizes that a Scrum-based board game can improve students’ understanding and performance in project management. An experimental study was conducted within a Master’s in Industrial Engineering program. A total of 112 students participated in the gamified activity (experimental group), while a control group followed traditional teaching methods. Both groups were assessed on their learning processes and exam performance. Results revealed that the experimental group showed significantly better comprehension of project management concepts, along with increased motivation and efficiency. This research offers empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of gamification in education. It also provides practical guidelines for implementing such tools in academic settings. By fostering innovative teaching practices, the study contributes to the ongoing development of engineering competencies. Furthermore, it presents a replicable model that can be adapted to business and management education, where project management skills and active learning strategies are equally critical.

papers.title: Automated Bayesian Optimization for Parameter Tuning of DE and PSO in Constrained Engineering Design under a Fixed Evaluation Budget
papers.abstract: Global optimization problems arise in many scientific and engineering domains and are often addressed using population-based metaheuristic algorithms. Among these, differential evolution (DE) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) are widely applied due to their robustness when handling nonconvex, black-box, and constrained objectives. The performance of DE and PSO strongly depends on how their parameters are set, yet these parameters are often selected by guessing and repeated testing rather than through an automatic optimization process. This study applies sequential model-based optimization (SMBO) with Gaussian process surrogates to systematically tune the parameters of DE and PSO under a fixed evaluation budget. The framework utilizes Matern and radial basis function (RBF) kernels within a Bayesian Optimization process (BO), supported by early stopping criteria to ensure efficient and reliable convergence. The approach is tested on three classical constrained engineering design problems: the welded beam (WBD), the pressure vessel (PVD), and the compression spring (CSD). Constraints are handled through a penalty formulation, and tuned configurations are compared with standard defaults across multiple independent trials under equalized evaluation budgets. Results show that SMBO-tuned DE and PSO achieve improved solution quality and reduced variability relative to their default counterparts. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of surrogate-based parameter tuning in improving the reliability, stability, and reproducibility of metaheuristic algorithms for real-world constrained global optimization problems.

papers.title: Enhancing RAG With Active Learning on Conversation Records: Reject Incapables and Answer Capables
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a key technique for leveraging external knowledge and enhancing the factual accuracy of large language models (LLMs). However, RAG still faces challenges in ensuring fully reliable responses in all scenarios. To address this, it is essential to identify samples that tend to lead to unreliable outputs or guide LLMs toward factually correct responses, which experts then annotate to develop high-quality datasets for refining LLMs. However, the growing scarcity of such datasets makes their creation challenging. This paper proposes using the vast amount of conversations generated from widespread LLM usage to build these datasets, with the goal of training LLMs to appropriately handle queries outside its capabilities while providing accurate responses to manageable ones. Given the impracticality of having experts annotate all conversation records, we introduce AL4RAG, a framework that uses active learning to select the most suitable conversation samples for annotation, filtering out redundant or noisy interactions and thereby optimizing model performance within a limited annotation budget. Additionally, recognizing that traditional active learning methods are not fully compatible with RAG due to unsuitable distance metrics, we develop a novel sample distance measurement for RAG active learning. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently outperforms baselines across multiple metrics.

papers.title: Long-Term Effects of Active Learning Seminar Education Based on Alumni Survey
papers.abstract: This study examines the long-term effects of active-learning-based professional seminar education using an alumni survey. Alumni of a research laboratory in a social science faculty at a public university were asked to rate on a five-point scale the extent to which their seminar education was useful in their professional lives. Ratings of 4 (“useful”) and 5 (“very useful”) accounted for approximately 90% of all responses, indicating that nearly all alumni evaluated the seminar education positively. However, aggregate data alone cannot provide sufficient information on educational effectiveness. The underlying meanings may differ, even within positive evaluations. This study examines the internal structure of these responses using free-text data from the alumni survey. The results revealed no significant differences between the rating-4 and rating-5 groups in terms of the specific work contexts in which learning was applied; however, qualitative differences were found in how learning was contextualized. Furthermore, these differences were related to career stage. In the early career stage, learning tended to be understood as an individual task performance capability, whereas in the approaching-mid-career stage, it was reinterpreted in terms of coordination and collaboration within and outside the organization. This study demonstrates the potential of utilizing alumni data in institutional research.

papers.title: Active Learning Career Modules Development and Its Impact on Students' Test Scores
papers.abstract: This study explores the development and impact of Active Learning Career Modules (ALCMs) on students’ test scores in career education. Career education faces challenges, particularly in China, where test scores in this field often lag behind those in traditional academic disciplines. This issue is exacerbated by passive, lecture-based teaching methods that fail to engage students or foster meaningful learning. To address this, the study proposes a series of modules incorporating active learning strategies such as collaborative learning, project-based learning (PBL), inquiry-based learning, flipped classrooms, and peer teaching and evaluation. The design of these modules integrates key learning theories, including Constructivist Theory, Behaviorist Learning Theory, Cognitive Learning Theory, and Cognitive Processing Theory, offering a comprehensive approach to improving student engagement, cognitive processes, and, ultimately, test scores. The study argues that these active learning strategies enhance student understanding, critical thinking, and real-world application, leading to measurable improvements in academic performance. The implications for teaching include a shift toward more interactive and student-centered learning environments, while recommendations for policymakers include incorporating these strategies into career education curricula. Future research could examine the long-term effects of these modules on career success and explore how the modules can be adapted for diverse student populations to further enhance academic outcomes.

papers.title: Prior-knowledge-infused neural network framework for experimental design of stochastic hybrid simulation
papers.abstract: Stochastic Hybrid Simulation (SHS) requires reliable prediction of structural responses to quantify uncertainties, yet conducting repeated runs via nonlinear time-history analysis or shaking-table testing is computationally or experimentally prohibitive. Although neural networks show promise for nonlinear response prediction, they struggle under the extremely limited high-fidelity data typical of experimental substructures in SHS. While Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) reduce data demands, they strictly rely on governing equations, which often fail to capture the complex, unmodeled nonlinearities (e.g., friction, noise) inherent in real physical specimens. Consequently, existing methods face challenges in accurately modeling experimental substructures. In this study, a Prior-Knowledge-Infused Neural Network (PKNN) is developed as a high-fidelity surrogate to replace the physical substructure in SHS. A two-stage training strategy is proposed: the network is first pretrained using abundant data from a simplified numerical model to learn fundamental physical laws, and subsequently fine-tuned with scarce shaking-table measurements to correct the physics-based bias and capture complex realistic behaviors. A 1/3-scale steel frame is used to evaluate the approach, predicting maximum inter-story drift ratios under varying structural parameters and ground-motion intensities. Results indicate that, in data-scarce regimes, PKNN maintains significantly higher predictive stability and accuracy than conventional neural networks or polynomial chaos expansions. These findings suggest that embedding simplified physics through pretraining offers a practical means to reduce the demand for high-fidelity data while retaining the ability to model nonlinear response and offers a robust pathway for SHS-oriented experimental design and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Lattice Structure, Optical Emission, and Photocatalytic Response of ZnO Nanoparticles Synthesized via Green Route
papers.abstract: Abstract This study emphasized the green synthesis of zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles utilizing the leaf extract of Camphora, which served as a natural reducing agent and stabilizer for the ZnO nanoparticles. The developed ZnO nanoparticles were characterized by several analytical techniques including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy (UV–Visible), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential (ZE), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and photoluminescence (PL). The XRD results confirmed that the ZnO nanoparticles were hexagonal wurtzite crystal structure with an average crystallite size of approximately 13 nm. Meanwhile, TEM analysis revealed that the nanoparticles are quasi-spherical in shape with an average diameter of 16 nm, indicating successful nanoparticle formation with a uniform morphology. The UV–Visible analysis showed a strong absorption peak at 334 nm, corresponding to a widened bandgap of 3.7 eV due to quantum confinement. FTIR spectra confirmed the involvement of phytochemicals in nanoparticles formation and stabilization. BET analysis indicated mesoporosity with predominate pore diameter of 35–40 nm, enhancing surface reactivity. Photocatalytic activity was evaluated against methylene blue (MB) dye under sunlight, where the ZnO nanoparticles achieved 97% degradation within 90 min. The high efficiency was attributed to nanoscale dimensions, oxygen vacancies and enhanced generation of reactive oxygen species. Importantly, reusability tests demonstrated sustained performance with 92% efficiency retained after five cycles. These findings highlight Camphora mediated ZnO nanoparticles as eco-friendly, stable and highly efficient photocatalysts for potential applications in wastewater treatment and environmental remediation.

papers.title: A Bayesian Approach to Feedback Control for Hyperbolic Balance Laws
papers.abstract: We propose a Bayesian framework for feedback boundary control of hyperbolic balance laws. The method propagates a probability distribution over feedback parameters using Lyapunov decay estimates as a likelihood. For linear models, it recovers available analytical stability results and extends to nonlinear regimes where theory is limited. Using first-order local Lax-Friedrichs (LLF) discretisations, we validate the approach on the decoupled wave system and the linearised Saint-Venant equations, reproducing known stability intervals and mixed boundary couplings. We then treat nonlinear and stochastic problems, including the nonlinear Saint-Venant system, one- and two-dimensional Burgers equations, Burgers equation with random initial data, and nonconservative perturbations with source terms, and show that the inferred stability domains are robust with respect to the indicator and the prior. Finally, we demonstrate transfer to a second-order semi-discrete LLF scheme and to a two-parameter feedback model for laser powder bed fusion with power regulation.

papers.title: A Unified PINN–SAC–SMC Framework for Adaptive Virtual Inertia Control and Real-Time Cyber-Attack Detection in Renewable Microgrids
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of inverter-based renewable energy sources reduces effective system inertia in modern microgrids, leading to faster frequency dynamics and increased vulnerability to disturbances and cyber-attacks. This paper proposes a unified Physics-Informed Neural Network–Soft Actor–Critic–Sliding Mode Control (PINN–SAC–SMC) framework for adaptive virtual inertia control, frequency regulation, and real-time cyber-attack detection. A physics-informed neural network (PINN) embeds swing-equation dynamics to generate a residual signal, which is used for anomaly detection and to guide a Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) agent in adaptively tuning virtual inertia. In parallel, a sliding mode control (SMC) layer ensures robust disturbance rejection and accurate frequency tracking in the presence of system uncertainties. System stability is rigorously established using Lyapunov analysis, yielding an ultimate frequency-deviation bound of 4.06 mHz. Polytopic eigenvalue analysis confirms local asymptotic stability over the inertia range $H_{v}\in [{2,10}]$ s, with a minimum damping ratio of 0.271, while frequency-domain analysis further verifies adequate gain and phase margins. The proposed framework is validated across six disturbance scenarios (S1–S6), achieving up to a 44% reduction in integral absolute error (IAE) compared to advanced baseline controllers. Ablation studies further demonstrate performance improvements of 44.1% and 37.3% relative to SMC-only and PINN-only configurations, respectively. In addition, the embedded detection mechanism achieves 99.51% accuracy, a 0.10% false-alarm rate, and detection delays of 4–11 ms across multiple cyber-attack types. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a unified and robust framework for enhancing both frequency stability and cyber-resilience in low-inertia microgrids.

papers.title: Improvement of Drone Gimbal System Performance Using a Parallel Structure of Explicit Model Predictive Control and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System
papers.abstract: Gimbal control is a crucial technology for drones that ensures camera stabilization and precise control of shooting angles, thereby enhancing the performance of unmanned aerial applications. The performance of the gimbal system is influenced by the motor inertia and external disturbances. In this study, the control performance of the gimbal system is improved using explicit model predictive control (EMPC), with external disturbances compensated by an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS). EMPC divides the control domain into polyhedral regions and calculates the control input by applying an optimal control law within each region. ANFIS is a control technique that integrates fuzzy logic with artificial neural networks. ANFIS learns the relationship between the inputs and outputs from the training data to construct a rule-based system. This study proposes a controller design methodology that connects EMPC and ANFIS in a parallel structure. ANFIS estimates and compensates for disturbances at each sampling interval. Since EMPC utilizes precomputed control laws based on critical regions, the parallel configuration with ANFIS reduces the computational complexity. Additionally, EMPC predicts the system’s behavior using a plant model and applies constraints, ensuring that the overall system remains stable and operates within a predictable range, even as ANFIS compensates for disturbances. To the best knowledge of the authors, this study presents the first experimental application of a parallel EMPC–ANFIS structure on a QUBE-Servo 3 drone gimbal system.

papers.title: Capsular Repair Matters for Residual Micromotion After Latarjet. An Externally Controlled Trial from the La Tour Group
papers.abstract: Background: Even though surgery is commonly used to treat glenohumeral instability, there is no evidence that such treatment effectively corrects glenohumeral translation. Purpose: This study aimed to analyze the effect of a new capsular reconstruction on residual micromotion after Latarjet procedure. Methods: Bilateral glenohumeral translation was assessed in nine patients preoperatively and one year postoperatively following Latarjet with a new capsular reconstruction (treatment group). Translation was measured using optical motion capture, computer tomography (CT) reconstructions, and 3- dimensional (3D) simulation. The results were compared with a previous cohort of eleven patients operated with traditional capsular reconstruction (control group). Results: A total of 20 patients were included in this study. The median follow-up duration was 12 months (range, 12 to 16 months). A statistically significant improvement in shoulder pain and function was reported postoperatively in treatment and control groups. No patients reported recurrent dislocation during the study period or had a positive apprehension sign at the final follow-up. The preoperative to postoperative range of motion (ROM) improvement was more pronounced in the treatment group than the control group with respect to shoulder flexion (P = .001), abduction (P = .041), and internal rotation with elbow at side (P = .035) for thoracohumeral motion, and shoulder abduction (P = .037), and internal rotation at 90/90 position (P = .006) for glenohumeral motion. The treatment group also exhibited more significant preoperative to postoperative reduction in anteroposterior translation during shoulder internal and external rotation with the elbow at the side (P = .018 and .016, respectively). Conclusion: This study demonstrated that a new type of capsulolabral reconstruction during the Latarjet procedure could reduce residual anteroposterior micromotion compared with a previously used technique, without compromising postoperative ROM. Although no differences in clinical apprehension were observed between groups, these biomechanical findings support the hypothesis that careful capsular management may influence postoperative shoulder stability. Whether this effect translates into long-term clinical benefit remains to be established in larger studies with extended follow-up.

papers.abstract: This paper develops a new systematic control method of traffic signals for a traffic flow model represented by the burgers' cellular automaton in order to reduce traffic jams.First, we construct "the Burgers' cellular automaton traffic flow model (BCATFM)," which is an ultradiscrete-type traffic flow model, and formulate an optimal traffic signal control problem for the BCATFM with a cost function defined by the total number of the traffic jam for the model as a nonlinear integer programming problem.Next, in order to solve the optimization problem, we propose an optimal switching algorithm of traffic signals based on particle swarm optimization, and derives an extended algorithm for disturbances on inflow/outflow of cars based on model predictive control.Then, some numerical simulations show that the new traffic signal control methods can reduce the total number of the traffic jam in comparison with other methods, and hence it is effective.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control of Offshore Wind Power Grid‐Tied Inverter Based on Inductance Parameter Identification and Grid Frequency Deviation Suppression
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To enhance the parameter robustness of model predictive control for grid‐tied inverters in offshore wind power grid‐tied systems, an advanced inductance identification method based on a minimum‐order state observer is proposed. First, an improved grid voltage observer with merely one gain parameter is designed. Besides, an inductance identification approach based on a grid voltage observer is proposed. Second, a thorough analysis of the observer characteristics is carried out. It is discovered that by adjusting the observer gain, a trade‐off can be achieved: a larger gain accelerates the dynamic convergence speed, while a smaller one fortifies its robustness against grid frequency deviations. This offers valuable guidance for parameter design. Finally, comparative experimental studies are conducted, which validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the robustness of model predictive control parameters.

papers.title: Hybrid Model Predictive Control with Adaptive Modulation for Voltage Balancing in Three-Phase Three-Level NPC Rectifiers for Green Hydrogen Production
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid model predictive control (HMPC) strategy for a three-level neutral-point-clamped (3L NPC) rectifier to optimize the operation of electrolyzers for green hydrogen production. Unlike conventional approaches that focus primarily on inverter applications, the proposed method directly addresses the critical issue of neutral-point voltage imbalance in NPC rectifiers. The control framework combines discrete switching-state selection with adaptive objective prioritization, utilizing real-time capacitor voltage measurements to exploit switching-state redundancy. A multi-objective cost function balances current tracking, DC-link voltage regulation, neutral-point voltage balancing, and switching-loss minimization. An adaptive weighting mechanism dynamically prioritizes control objectives in response to system conditions such as renewable intermittency and grid disturbances. To improve long-term reliability, the strategy introduces state diversity enforcement and inactivity penalties, reducing capacitor stress without compromising harmonic performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using a dynamic equivalent model of a proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer, enabling a realistic assessment of green hydrogen production. Validation through hardware in the loop (HIL) test demonstrates robust current control and stable DC-link voltages in varying operating scenarios.

papers.title: Optimal Multi-timescale Model Predictive Control-based Power Allocation of Hybrid Energy Storage Systems via Reference Curve Tracking
papers.abstract: The intermittency of renewable energy has made stable power supply a focal and challenging research topic in today’s power system. However, most existing intelligenceenabled control protocols pose significant computational complexity, hindering their practical applications in multitimescale power control scenarios. This paper proposes an optimal power allocation method for hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) based on complementary power reference curves. The approach leverages batteries’ dynamic characteristics and output properties and algorithmic features to construct complementary power reference curves. Through real-time tracking of these reference curves, the method achieves coordinated and stable power output across multiple timescales. The improved model predictive control (MPC) is integrated into the control strategy to efficiently convert power tracking into current prediction. This approach enhances system dynamic response without needing excessive computational resources. Furthermore, the proposed method is integrated into a dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) for power quality control. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through hardware experiments.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization-enhanced machine learning axial load prediction across diverse CFST columns, strengths, geometries, and slenderness
papers.abstract: Concrete-filled steel tubes (CFST) are recognized for their superior structural performance, offering enhanced strength, ductility, and construction efficiency. This enhanced performance is primarily due to the synergistic relationship between the steel casing and the concrete core; the steel imparts confinement to the concrete, thereby augmenting its compressive strength and ductility, while the concrete infill simultaneously restrains the steel tube against local buckling. This study addresses the critical need for accurate prediction of axial compression capacity in diverse CFST columns, spanning both circular and rectangular cross-sections, and encompassing short to slender configurations. A key focus was accommodating a wide range of material strengths, from conventional normal concrete and steel to contemporary ultra-high-performance concrete and high-strength steel. To achieve this, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms specifically, ExtraTrees, XGBoost, and GradientBoosting, were employed. The hyperparameters of these models were optimized using Bayesian Optimization to maximize predictive efficacy. The developed models were rigorously validated through 10-fold cross-validation, demonstrating high accuracy, with coefficients of determination (R²) achieving up to 0.99 in predicting CFST column failure loads. Comprehensive error and sensitivity analyses were conducted to thoroughly assess their predictive capabilities and robustness. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was utilized to elucidate model decision-making processes and identify the most influential input parameters, enhancing interpretability and confidence. This research significantly advances the efficient, reliable, and data-informed design of CFST structures, expanding their applicability and fostering greater industry acceptance, particularly for innovative designs utilizing high-performance materials.

papers.title: Adaptive Digital Twin Modeling with Control : Integration of Extended Kalman Filter-Based Recursive Sparse Nonlinear Identification with Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: The adoption of digital twins has revolutionized industrial process simulation, monitoring, and control effectiveness. However, practical implementations of digital twins are hindered by substantial challenges, including extended development time, diminishing model accuracy, and restricted interactive capabilities. Addressing these critical issues, this paper proposes a comprehensive digital twin development framework that integrates digital twin identification, real-time model updating, and advanced process control. The proposed approach first identifies the offline digital twin model through the sparse identification of a nonlinear dynamics algorithm, reducing the digital twin development time while maintaining model fidelity. Then, the identified model is updated by the extended Kalman filter to mitigate the problem of diminishing accuracy. Finally, incorporating the latest updated model into the model predictive control facilitates the control inputs optimization and enhances the interactive capacity of digital twins. Through one industrial case study and two simulation examples, the advantages of the proposed algorithm are demonstrated.

papers.title: A Dynamic Decoupling Method for Composite Gearbox Faults Based on an Improved CPO-VMD and Bayesian Optimization Dual-Filter Approach
papers.abstract: To address the issues of strong noise interference, low decoupling accuracy, and poor separation efficiency in gearbox composite fault diagnosis, this paper proposes an improved CPO-VMD and Bayesian optimization (BO) dual-filter-based dynamic decoupling method for weak composite gearbox faults (ICPO-BFDD). First, the crown porcupine optimization (CPO) algorithm is enhanced by incorporating average permutation entropy (APE) as the fitness function to adaptively select the optimal parameters of variational modal decomposition (VMD). Compared with other metaheuristics, the improved CPO (ICPO) achieves the lowest MAPE (0.83814) and converges at the 4th iteration. Moreover, the resulting ICPO-VMD yields higher SNR and lower RMSE than conventional decomposition methods such as empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD) under the same noise conditions, while preserving time-domain fluctuation patterns, frequency-domain energy distribution, and periodic fault impact characteristics. Second, a fast spectral kurtosis map is constructed from the denoised signal to identify the core fault-related frequency band. Using spectral peak salience entropy (SPSE) as the objective function, BO adaptively designs a dual bandpass-bandstop filter bank, enabling precise separation of weakly coupled composite faults with different coupling strengths. Compared with typical decoupling methods such as fast spectral kurtosis deconvolution (FSKD) and independent component analysis (ICA), the proposed BO-driven dual-filter bank achieves higher separation accuracy, delivering an SNR improvement of 3.7 dB over FSKD and an RMSE reduction of 16.7% compared with ICA on simulated signals. Finally, a closed-loop “decomposition-denoising-decoupling” optimization system is established, which dynamically updates parameters and continuously optimizes decoupling performance. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in noise suppression and fault feature extraction, with superior fault feature visibility verified via qualitative envelope spectrum analysis for practically measured gearbox signals.

papers.title: A Bayesian‐Optimized Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for Automated Detection and Classification of Retinal Diseases in Ghana Using OCT Images
papers.abstract: Retinal diseases pose a significant global health challenge due to their potential to cause severe visual impairment and blindness. This study aimed to develop a robust deep learning ensemble framework for the automated detection and classification of retinal diseases from optical coherence tomography (OCT) images. This study used OCT images from WATBORG Eye Services in Ghana, including glaucoma, macular edema, posterior vitreous detachment (PVD), and healthy eyes. The data preprocessing steps included augmentation, resizing, and one‐hot encoding. The dataset was divided into training (56%), validation (14%), and testing (30%) sets using stratified sampling. Six convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, Visual Geometry Group (VGG)‐16, VGG19, DenseNet121, MobileNet, ResNet50, and InceptionV3, were evaluated as base models. To optimize hyperparameters for each model, Gaussian process–based Bayesian optimization was used. In addition to analyzing individual architectures, two ensemble learning strategies, soft ensemble and stacked ensemble, were implemented to combine the predictions from the models. Among the six base learners, VGG16, VGG19, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, MobileNet, and ResNet50‐VGG19 achieved the highest individual accuracy of 97.74%, followed by MobileNet (93.99%), InceptionV3 (93.61%), DenseNet121 (93.23%), VGG16 (91.73%), and ResNet50 (60.53%). The ensemble strategies outperformed most single models. The soft ensemble achieved an accuracy of 95.11% with high precision, recall, and specificity, indicating improved stability and reduced variance across disease categories. The stacked ensemble yielded the best overall results, achieving an accuracy of 97.37%, a precision of 97.78%, a recall of 97.93%, an F 1‐score of 97.85%, and a ROC–AUC of 0.9993. Bootstrap resampling was incorporated to assess the stability and reliability of the reported performance. This study demonstrates that integrating Bayesian‐optimized CNN architectures with ensemble learning significantly enhances retinal disease classification performance. By applying these methods to a Ghanaian dataset—an underrepresented population in retinal artificial intelligence (AI) research—this work highlights the potential of AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimize resource allocation, and promote health equity in ophthalmic care. Future research should focus on scaling datasets, integrating multimodal data, and conducting clinical validations to support the real‐world deployment of these models.

papers.title: Pre-trained Invertible Neural Network Assisted High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization Framework for Wind Farm Layout Design
papers.abstract: Wake effects in wind farms degrade energy capture and turbine reliability, underscoring the importance of layout optimization. Existing studies either rely on analytical wake models at the expense of accuracy or combine numerical wake models with heuristic algorithms at the expense of efficiency. In contrast, we propose a pre-trained invertible neural network assisted high-dimensional Bayesian optimization framework for wind farm layout design, achieving both high accuracy and high efficiency. Specifically, this study employs a high-fidelity numerical wake model to ensure accurate wake estimation and develops a Bayesian optimization (BO)–based framework to enhance search efficiency. An invertible neural network (INN) is specifically designed and, for the first time, integrated with BO to alleviate the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional layout spaces. The proposed INN-BO framework is evaluated under five distinct and progressively complex scenarios, including the real offshore data from California. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art algorithms demonstrate that INN-BO achieves superior solution quality with reduced convergence time, highlighting its strong generalizability and practical relevance to real-world wind farm design.

papers.title: A Micromotion Feature Extraction Method for Rotor UAVs Based on Sinusoidal Frequency Modulation Basis Under Strong Clutter Background
papers.abstract: The micro-motion characteristics of rotor UAVs reflect the small movements and attitude changes during flight, which can provide important information for identification and distinction. Existing methods mainly utilize the echo frequency-domain representation to extract the micro-motion features of rotor UAVs. However, the performance of such methods deteriorates sharply under strong clutter background, because echo frequency domain is submerged by noise. In this article, a micro motion feature extraction method for rotor UAVs based on sinusoidal frequency modulation basis under strong clutter background is proposed. Firstly, the projection coefficient properties of rotor UAVs echoes on sinusoidal frequency modulated basis are studied. The expression and statistical properties of the coefficients are derived. The maximum variance of the projection coefficients on the sinusoidal frequency modulation basis is used to extract the target rotation frequency and the number of blades. Then, the blade length is extracted according to the coefficient properties. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by the simulation and measured data.

papers.title: Physics-informed stochastic models for theme park ride waiting times
papers.abstract: A stochastic model for theme park ride waiting times is developed by modeling the waiting time as a continuous-time, discrete-state Markov process with state-dependent, time-varying transition rates. These transition rates are interpreted as a control term acting on the waiting-time process, allowing the model calibration task to be formulated as a data-driven optimal control problem. To solve this problem efficiently, we construct a physics-informed neural network (PINN) that embeds the Kolmogorov forward equation solver into its architecture. Under mild assumptions, we prove the existence of an optimal control, providing theoretical support for the learning procedure. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the PINN-based solution. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, physically consistent, and data-driven approach for modeling and forecasting ride waiting times.

papers.title: Geometric-Semantic Diversity-Aware Active Learning for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing
papers.abstract: Oriented object detection in aerial remote sensing imagery faces challenges of costly annotation due to dense object distributions and complex geometric variations. Active learning (AL) offers an effective approach to mitigate annotation costs by selectively labeling the most informative samples. However, existing AL methods predominantly focus on uncertainty or rep resentativeness criteria independently, lacking sufficient consideration for geometric and semantic diversity, which is especially important for rotated objects in remote sensing scenarios. To address these issues, we propose a Geometric-Semantic Diversity aware Active Learning (GSD-AL) framework for oriented object detection. Specifically, our method integrates instance-level un certainty with both geometric and semantic diversity constraints. The Geometric Diversity Module (GDM) exploits the spatial variability of rotated bounding boxes, emphasizing diversity in aspect ratios and rotation angles to avoid redundancy. Concurrently, the Semantic Diversity Module (SDM) computes cosine similarity based on PCA-reduced features, enabling efficient instance filtering to ensure semantic representativeness. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic class-balancing strategy that prioritizes uncertain samples from minority classes through the enforcement of class-specific sampling limits. Extensive experiments conducted on two publicly available datasets demonstrate that our proposed GSD-AL framework reduces annotation costs while achieving superior detection performance compared to state-of-the-art AL methods. Specifically, our method achieves a state-of-the-art 70.7% mAP using only 20,000 labeled instances, outperforming the next-best method by 1.9% under the same annotation budget on the DOTA-v1.0 dataset. The code is accessible at: https://github.com/wangyue377/GSD-AL.

They extend classical world models by describing the state of an environment based on information that has a tangible meaning for humans. This includes, for example, the class membership of objects located within the environment and their spatial relationship. Thus, semantic models bridge the gap between humans and robots and open up new possibilities for the industrial application of mobile robotics. In this paper, a software architecture is presented that implements a semantic world model focusing on the localization and identification of object instances.

papers.title: Incommensurate fractional epidemic dynamics with compartment-specific memory, treatment response, and physics-informed forecasting
papers.abstract: This paper develops an incommensurate fractional-order susceptible-exposed-symptomatic infectious-asymptomatic infectious-treated-recovered (SEIATR) model with compartment-specific Caputo memory. We establish local well-posedness, positivity, boundedness, biological feasibility, disease-free and endemic equilibria, and the basic reproduction number. Local stability is analyzed through the rational-order incommensurate Matignon criterion. A componentwise multi-order L1 scheme is then used for simulation, refinement, and sensitivity analysis. Finally, a physics-informed neural network is employed as a synthetic benchmark for hidden-state reconstruction, parameter and order identification, residual checking, and short-horizon forecasting. The results show that compartment-specific memory mainly affects peak timing, persistence, and treatment load, whereas epidemiological rates govern amplification and threshold behavior.

papers.title: WORLD MODELS AND EMBODIED AI FOR ROBOTICS: BRIDGING SIMULATION AND REALITY
papers.abstract: World models represent a transformative approach in robotics by enabling AI systems to build internal predictive representations of physical environments. Unlike large language models that excel at linguistic pattern matching, world models understand spatial relationships, physics dynamics, and causal interactions critical for embodied agents. This paper examines recent advances in world model architectures for robotic applications, analyzing how systems like Google DeepMind's Genie 3, NVIDIA's Cosmos, and Microsoft's Rho-alpha enable zero-shot task generalization, simulation-to-reality transfer, and multimodal sensory integration. We synthesize 2025-2026 developments demonstrating that world models reduce real-world robot training requirements by 50-90% while enabling unprecedented versatility in manipulation, navigation, and human-robot interaction. Key applications span disaster response, manufacturing automation, and service robotics. Technical challenges including verification of causal understanding, real-time computational demands, and integration with language-based reasoning are critically evaluated. Evidence indicates world models constitute essential infrastructure for achieving reliable, adaptive embodied intelligence in dynamic real-world contexts.

papers.title: Deriving a Data-Efficient, Generalist Agent Through World Models
papers.abstract: Machine learning researchers long to derive a generalist agent whose problem-solving abilities span over multiple tasks. At the same time, we are also interested in data efficiency, i.e., training agents with fewer, limited training samples. To these two distinctive ends, recent lines of research on world models (WMs) for image-based reinforcement learning (RL) tasks have also shown a stark divergence. The first line is to scale a singular world model to operate on many environments at the cost of requiring billions of training experiences. The second focuses on training one specialized world model per environment, but within a limited budget of one hundred thousand (100k) interactions. In this research, we propose mae, the transformer WM agent that thrives in both ends, i.e., operates in multiple environments using a single set of backbone world model parameters with the limited hundred thousand (100k) training samples per environment. On the standard Atari 100k benchmark, we achieve superhuman performance in 9 of the 26 games, obtaining human-normalized mean, interquartile mean (IQM), and median scores of 1.15, 0.56, and 0.46, respectively, using a single WM backbone across all games and game-specific RL networks. While competitive, these scores fall modestly short of specialized, game-specific transformer WM agents. Remarkably, mae learns a rewarding policy without observing any positive reward in the target environment, and ablations provide evidence of cross-environment transfer. Lastly, we validate mae’s applicability in a 3D, first-person view environment with a long-horizon task.

papers.title: CytoAL: Toward Label-Efficient Cytology Diagnosis via Cellularity-Guided Active Learning
papers.abstract: Examining thyroid fine needle aspiration (FNA) can grade cancer risks, derive prognostic information, and guide follow-up care or surgery decision-making. However, thyroid cytology's diagnostic cues are more dispersed compared with pathology images in other disciplines, making standard annotation strategy for AI diagnosis labor-intensive. Inspired by how cytologists diagnose under the microscope, we propose an innovative cellularity-based active learning framework, namely Cyto-AL, to correlate cellularity with diagnostic categories for the active learning query. We also improve the Whole Slide Image (WSI) category of The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytology (TBSRTC) prediction by proposing severe-stage pinpointed Multiple Instance Learning (MIL). Additionally, we introduce a lightweight score model to optimize the query in human in the loop (HITL) annotation strategy. Given scarce public thyroid cytology datasets, we release our collected and labeled images as benchmarks. The benchmark comprises 138 WSIs (27,496 valid image patches) collected from 2021-2023 across six classes, annotated by three pathologists using TBSRTC. At patch-level verification, Cyto-AL achieves a 2.2% average classification accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art methods with an equally labeled dataset, and its lightweight ranking-aware model reduces training time by around 65%. Moreover, the WSI-level MIL approach improves average accuracy by 10.7% and Macro-F1 score by 3.5%, outperforming standard sampling methods such as Monte Carlo sampling. The source code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Junchao-Zhu/Cyto-AL.

papers.title: Spatter Reduction in Coherent Beam Combining Laser Welding of Aluminum through Intensity Distribution and Deflection Frequency Adjustment for Low Penetration Wide Welds in Transition Mode
papers.abstract: Aluminum is an important material for lightweight construction and is particularly environmentally friendly due to its 100 percent recyclability. However, unstable melt pools and keyholes of this material make it more susceptible to spatter during laser beam welding. Proven methods to stabilize the melt pool and reduce spatter are focus adjustments, beam oscillation or tailored beam shapes. Using Coherent Beam Combining (CBC), Dynamic Beam Lasers (DBL) can push a wide variety of intensity distributions with different oscillation frequencies on top of the melt pool, that can stabilize the melt pool and control the keyhole dynamics. This can further help not only to achieve a spatter free weld, but also to aim for a very low penetration depth, suitable for special welding scenarios like laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) or foils in electromobility. This study investigates the general suitability of complex DBL systems with dynamic intensity distribution for spatter-free transition mode welding of aluminum flat seams in different frequency ranges. The evaluation of high-speed imaging and weld quality, including metallographic examination, is presented and discussed.

papers.title: Annotation-efficient Semi-supervised and Active Learning for Breast Cancer Segmentation in DCE-MRI
papers.abstract: Accurate breast tumor segmentation in dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) is vital for diagnosis and treatment planning. Despite advances in deep learning, its performance remains constrained by the need for extensive voxel-wise annotations. To mitigate this burden, we propose an annotation-efficient framework that jointly optimizes data selection, unlabeled data utilization, and data augmentation under limited annotation budgets. A diversity-aware uncertainty query (DUQ) strategy guides the annotation by jointly modeling data representativeness and informativeness through a representative candidate selector (RCS) and an uncertainty-based decision maker (UDM), ensuring efficient and targeted labeling. To leverage unlabeled data, a cross-decoder consistency regularization (CDCR) mechanism enforces prediction consistency between two decoders with distinct attention mechanisms, enhancing robustness and confidence. Furthermore, a lesion transplant augmentation (LTA) technique synthesizes anatomically valid pseudo samples by transplanting lesion regions from labeled to unlabeled images, effectively expanding training diversity. Experiments were conducted on two DCE-MRI datasets with biopsy-proven breast cancers, one as internal dataset containing 676 subjects and the other as external dataset with 344 subjects. Comparative and ablation results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised and active learning methods, providing a simple yet effective annotation-efficient solution for breast cancer segmentation in DCE-MRI. The code is publicly available at https: //github.com/zouquanling/DUQ_and_CDCR.

papers.title: Design and validation of a low-cost, modular cold stage for ice-templating and cryobioprinting applications
papers.abstract: Cryogenic platforms are increasingly vital in advanced manufacturing processes such as ice-templating and cryobioprinting, where precise subzero control enables novel material architectures and biofabrication strategies. However, commercial cold stages remain prohibitively expensive, bulky, and inflexible. These barriers limit experimentation, accessibility and integration in educational and research environments. This paper presents the design and validation of a low-cost, open-hardware cold stage capable of reaching –30 °C in ambient conditions and – 50 °C in a refrigerated enclosure, supporting samples up to 80 × 80 mm. Developed using off-the-shelf components and rapid prototyping techniques, the system exemplifies how design-for-affordability and modularity can democratize access to advanced manufacturing tools. The architecture combines a two-stage thermoelectric cooling system, precision temperature sensing and real-time control via an Arduino-based PID loop, all housed in a structure fabricated through extrusion-based 3D bioprinting, with a total cost under €550. Beyond its technical performance, comparable to commercial systems at a fraction of the cost, this platform serves as a case study in design-driven innovation. It highlights how open-source principles, digital fabrication and iterative prototyping can accelerate the development of specialized manufacturing equipment. The system has been deployed in both research and educational settings, enabling hands-on learning in thermal control systems and biofabrication. This work demonstrates how low-cost, adaptable tools can expand the frontiers of manufacturing research and education. The design is fully documented and reproducible, offering a scalable foundation for future enhancements, including integration with multi-extrusion and contour printing capabilities for thermo-sensitive and photocurable hydrogels towards complex tissue fabrication.

papers.title: Effect of spatial power distribution on resulting microstructure in H13 tool steel
papers.abstract: This study investigated the influence of spatial power distributions, featuring a concentric core and ring beam, on seam geometry and microstructural evolution in bead on plate welds produced on H13 hot-work tool steel. Single-track seams were generated using core-dominated, balanced core-ring and ring-dominated power distributions at identical power-velocity combinations relevant for Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF, PBF-LB/M). Microstructural analysis of the resulting weld seams revealed that Gaussian-like beam profiles consistently led to pronounced microstructural heterogeneity, characterized by the coexistence of a fine cellular type microstructure in the upper region and a whisker-like type microstructure near the weld seam bottom. In contrast, redistribution of laser power based on core-ring beam profiles resulted in a progressive reduction of the whisker-like type microstructure. For the ring-dominated power distributions, the weld seams exhibited a predominantly homogeneous cellular type microstructure across all investigated process parameters. The results demonstrate that the spatial power distribution of the laser beam plays a decisive role in governing microstructural evolution in laser-processed H13, exceeding the influence of melt pool geometry alone. Laser beam shaping therefore represents an effective process-based strategy for controlling microstructural heterogeneity and improving the processability of crack-sensitive tool steels.

papers.title: Refined State-error-based Model Predictive Control and Flight Testing of Eagle of Taihu 10: A Canard-Configured Tail-Sitter Technology Demonstrator
papers.abstract: As the size of tail-sitter electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft increases, significant challenges have arisen due to a lower thrust-to-weight ratio, more nonlinear aerodynamics during transition, and slower control response. To support the design and implementation of the flight control system for the large-scale tail-sitter eVTOL Eagle of Taihu 100 (ET100), a one-third-scale, 13 kg subscale technology demonstrator, ET10, was developed. This paper presents the control framework tailored for ET series. In this framework, a refined state-error-based model predictive control (MPC) scheme is proposed. By reformulating the translational dynamics, the coupling between translation and rotation is explicitly captured. Aerodynamic feedforward and efficiency-aware control allocation are integrated to mitigate model uncertainties. A PX4 software-in-the-loop (SITL) platform was constructed by integrating data from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and experiments to ensure a high-fidelity aerodynamic modeling. Flight simulations were first conducted to evaluate the improved algorithm in terms of tracking performance across various tasks. Next, flight tests of the ET10 were conducted, demonstrating the reliability and robustness of the scheme across the full flight envelope.

papers.title: Real-Time Multimodal Attention-State Classification on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices via Hardware-Aware CNN With Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Real-time attention monitoring using physiological signals is critical for next-generation wearable healthcare and human–computer interaction systems. However, most existing approaches rely on computationally intensive models limiting their applicability in resource-constrained edge environments. This paper presents a hardware-aware multimodal deep learning framework for real-time attention-state classification using photoplethysmography (PPG) and galvanic skin response (GSR) signals. The proposed approach integrates a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization using Optuna’s Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE)-driven tuning to jointly optimize classification performance and embedded deployment efficiency. A novel end-to-end pipeline is developed that encompasses signal preprocessing, multimodal encoding, model optimization, and on-device inference on a low-power nRF52840 microcontroller-based platform. Offline evaluation on the PhyAAt dataset achieves a validation accuracy of 90.28%. In a preliminary single-subject on-device evaluation, the deployed INT8 model achieved 81.48% real-time accuracy (95% binomial exact confidence interval computed using the Clopper–Pearson method) with an average inference latency of 118 ms under strict memory constraints (48 kB Flash, 27 kB SRAM). The moderate performance degradation between offline and real-time settings demonstrates the robustness and practical feasibility of the proposed framework. Compared to existing multimodal and edge-AI approaches, the proposed system explicitly balances accuracy, latency, and memory footprint, enabling continuous on-device attention monitoring without reliance on cloud infrastructure. This work establishes a scalable pathway toward low-power, privacy-preserving, and real-time cognitive state monitoring in wearable and IoT-based healthcare systems.

papers.title: Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Hybrid CNN-RNN: A Unified-Loop Hyperparameter Optimization Framework via Surrogate-Based Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: In bearing fault diagnosis for Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), the overall performance of data-driven models is strongly influenced by the coupled effects of preprocessing, model configuration, and decision fusion. However, these components are often optimized independently, resulting in fragmented workflows that limit global optimality, reproducibility, and computational efficiency of the model. This study presents a computationally unified three-stage sequential optimization framework that systematically coordinates the preprocessing selection, model hyperparameter optimization, and decision-level fusion within a consistent surrogate-based optimization architecture. In the first stage, candidate preprocessing schemes reflecting physical fault mechanisms—outer race, inner race, rolling element, and cage faults—are evaluated using a training-free Class Separability Score (CSS), which enables efficient screening without introducing model bias. In the second stage, the hyperparameters of two complementary architectures—an EfficientNetV2-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) operating in the time–frequency domain and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) operating in the time domain—are optimized independently by maximizing the cross-validated performance. In the third stage, a stacking-based late fusion model is constructed using out-of-fold posterior probabilities to learn the optimal decision rules that exploit cross-model complementarity. All stages are governed by a unified optimization container integrating Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS), Kriging surrogate modeling with expected improvement, and Bayesian Optimization with Hyperband (BOHB), enabling surrogate-assisted exploration under multi-fidelity computational budgets. Numerical experiments on benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and MAFAULDA, demonstrate the stable convergence behavior of the sequential optimization process and consistent performance gains over single-model baselines. Reproducibility is ensured through fixed data partitions, random seeds, and normalization boundaries across all stages. The proposed framework provides a structured and reproducible computational modeling approach for bearing fault diagnosis, highlighting how coordinated optimization across multiple stages can improve the robustness and efficiency of complex PHM workflows.
