papers.title: Adaptive tracking control with Lyapunov regularization for data-calibrated Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy Markov jump biological systems
papers.abstract: Cancer–tumour–immune dynamics are nonlinear, uncertain, and subject to abrupt biological or treatment-induced regime changes. This paper develops a data-calibrated adaptive tracking-control framework for Takagi–Sugeno (T–S) fuzzy Markov jump biological systems with unknown local dynamics and unknown transition probabilities. The proposed method combines mode-dependent fitted Q iteration with a Lyapunov-penalized policy update, so that the learned controller uses transition data while remaining close to a bounded stabilizing reference action. For the sampled discounted problem, we establish Bellman contraction, well-posedness of the fitted regression update, an approximate fitted Q error bound, a quantitative Lyapunov-penalization bound, a practical tracking guarantee for the Lyapunov-regularized policy, and positivity preservation under projected states and dimensionless inputs. Public tumour-volume data associated with the FIR atezolizumab non-small-cell lung cancer study are used only to calibrate plausible tumour-growth ranges; a trajectory-level holdout split is applied to avoid in-sample reporting. In the resulting active-treatment simulation regime, the proposed controller gives the best overall balanced performance among the compared strategies, which now include proximal policy optimization (PPO), soft actor–critic (SAC), nominal model predictive control (MPC), local tracking feedback, reference-action control, fixed scheduling, non-switching fitted Q iteration, and no control. In the representative single-seed run, the Lyapunov-regularized fitted Q iteration (LR-FQI) method achieves low weighted cost ($ 51.17 $), low tumour integral squared error (ISE) ($ 1.70 $), short threshold-exceedance time ($ 4 $ days), and moderate total dimensionless input. A Monte Carlo evaluation over 50 independent Markov and noise trajectories gives the lowest mean weighted cost for the proposed controller ($ 47.29\pm19.91 $, mean $ \pm $ standard deviation) and a consistent threshold-exceedance time of $ 4.00\pm0.00 $ days. Assumption 4 is verified numerically over 5000 sampled domain points.

papers.title: Revisión sistemática de la multimodalidad en el aprendizaje del inglés en entornos híbridos.
papers.abstract: The teaching of English in higher education is currently conducted within hybrid environments that integrate both face-to-face and digital experiences. This shift has increased interest in multimodal approaches capable of incorporating visual, auditory, and kinesthetic resources into the learning process. In this context, the present systematic review aimed to analyze the scientific evidence published between 2019 and 2025 on multimodality applied to English language learning in hybrid university settings. The study was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and included articles retrieved from high-impact databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis Online, Redalyc, and Scielo. Following the processes of identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion, a total of 50 studies were selected for the final analysis. The findings indicate that the structured integration of multimodal resources enhances student motivation, engagement, reading comprehension, oral fluency, pronunciation, and learner autonomy in English language learning. Furthermore, three dominant trends were identified: the use of interactive digital tools to promote active learning, the incorporation of multisensory experiences to strengthen linguistic competencies, and the consolidation of hybrid models aimed at addressing diverse learning styles and needs. However, several limitations persist, including challenges related to teacher training, the digital divide, multimodal assessment, and the lack of standardized methodological criteria. It is concluded that multimodality represents a relevant and effective pedagogical strategy for English language learning in hybrid environments, provided that its implementation is grounded in contextualized, inclusive, and pedagogically coherent instructional design.

papers.title: Professional learning experiences of university Physical Education lecturers in digital technology
papers.abstract: Introduction: Quality Physical Education (PE) and sport education increasingly depend on lecturers’ capacity to integrate digital technology, manage pedagogical knowledge, and redesign active learning experiences that promote participation, collaboration, and reflective practice. Objective: This study explores how university physical education lecturers in Indonesia interpret digital technology and transformation as drivers of invention in PE teaching and professional learning. Methodology: We collected an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design from ninety-eight participants and analyzed the data thematically through professional development observations with follow-up semi-structured interviews on digital technology and transformation as well as technology-enabled pedagogy that creates supportive environmental conditions for learning. Results: The analysis discovered significant findings regarding how digital technology and transformation could enhance reflective PE practice and serve as developing for redesigning PE instruction, as well as for creating supportive environmental conditions in PE pedagogy. Discussion: The findings suggest that an effective managerial environment helps PE lecturers co-construct new teaching strategies that integrate technology with movement-based learning goals, aligning with calls for quality PE that advances inclusion, collaboration, and lifelong physical activity habits. Conclusions: Strengthening environmental support for digital technology and transformation in PE could improve lecturers’ professional learning, promote pedagogical invention, and improve the quality of physical education and sport education in higher education programs preparing future PE teachers.

papers.title: The Effect of Metacognition and Digital Literacy on Listening Skills in the Context of Foreign Language Learning
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the development of listening skills in a foreign-language context through the variables of metacognitive awareness and digital literacy. Listening is not a passive process limited to perceiving auditory input; rather, it is an active learning domain involving multi-layered cognitive operations such as lower-level linguistic decoding and higher-level meaning construction, inferencing, and maintaining discourse coherence. In this regard, how learners plan, monitor, and evaluate their listening processes constitutes a central determinant of listening success. The study was designed as a qualitative inquiry based on a descriptive review model and conducted using document analysis. National and international academic studies were systematically examined, and themes related to metacognitive strategies in listening, components of digital literacy, and the effects of digital listening environments on learning processes were analyzed through thematic analysis. The review results indicate that metacognitive awareness significantly supports listening skill development through planning, monitoring, and evaluation strategies that regulate the listening process. Findings further demonstrate that digital literacy plays a decisive role in the effective use of digital listening materials and strengthens the applicability of metacognitive strategies. Podcasts, online videos, and multimedia-supported listening content provide learners with process control; however, the efficient use of these opportunities appears closely related to learners’ levels of digital literacy and metacognitive awareness. Overall, the study highlights the pedagogical importance of integrating metacognitive strategy instruction and digital literacy-based approaches holistically in developing listening skills and provides a theoretical foundation for future empirical research.

papers.title: Towards low-cost surface inspection using artificial vision in practical industrial environments
papers.abstract: Surface inspection in the steel industry plays a crucial role in quality control, driving significant research efforts, particularly with the rise of deep learning models. However, many existing works focus on minor model variations that offer limited practical advantages and fail to address critical challenges such as lighting conditions and dataset curation. This paper presents a high-performance surface inspection system that integrates deep learning with real-time parallel processing to enhance defect detection in industrial settings. The proposed system employs a modular and scalable architecture based on a publish/subscribe messaging pattern, ensuring efficient data flow and seamless integration of components. It incorporates active learning methodologies and advanced image processing techniques, including color correction, light compensation, and contrast enhancement. Designed for industrial deployment, the system balances high performance with reduced installation costs and minimal maintenance by utilizing a single area-scan camera and AC illumination. The optimized positioning of the camera and lighting reduces surface reflections and motion blur, improving defect detection accuracy. The system achieves high-speed processing by parallelizing preprocessing and post-processing tasks, effectively minimizing computational overhead and enabling continuous real-time monitoring. A built-in performance monitoring module provides valuable insights for system optimization and real-time assessment. Extensive testing in a steel pickling line demonstrates the system's robustness and effectiveness in realistic industrial environments, offering a reliable and scalable solution for automated surface inspection.

papers.title: Impacts of Unfolding Case-Study Learning on Nursing Students' Performance Outcomes: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Introduction: The unfolding case study is an innovative teaching strategy that structures patient scenarios over time to enhance learner engagement and improve outcomes. However, its effectiveness in nursing education classroom settings worldwide remains underexplored. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the impact of unfolding case-study learning on nursing students' knowledge, critical thinking, and self-efficacy. Methods: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses- Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Searches covered CINAHL (EBSCOhost), Cochrane Library (Wiley), Embase (Elsevier), ERIC (IES), MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus (Elsevier), and Web of Science Core Collection (Clarivate) for English-language studies published from January 2012 to September 2025. Study appraisal used the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018) and NHMRC levels of evidence for quantitative designs. Results: The initial search identified 550 studies, of which 19 were included after rigorous screening. Findings indicated that unfolding case studies positively influenced knowledge acquisition by promoting active learning, enhancing integration of theory into practice, strengthening collaborative learning and communication, and improving long-term knowledge retention and recall. Evidence also supported improvements in critical thinking skills and self-efficacy among nursing students. Conclusion: Integrating unfolding case-based learning into undergraduate nursing education offers substantial advantages in developing essential skills, particularly knowledge acquisition, critical thinking, and self-efficacy.

papers.title: Bridging Pedagogy and Skills: Student-Centered Learning and Human-Centered Competencies in International Schools In Phnom Penh, Cambodia
papers.abstract: This study examined the extent of student-centered learning (SCL) strategies and the manifestation of human-centered competencies (HCC) among secondary students in selected international schools in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Employing a descriptive-correlational design, data were gathered from 77 secondary school teachers using a researcher-developed questionnaire assessing the five SCL dimensions: collaborative, inquiry-based, problem-based, active, and differentiated instruction; and the five HCC domains: critical thinking, creativity, communication, collaboration, and socio-emotional skills. Findings revealed that all SCL strategies were implemented at a high level (overall M = 3.98), with problem-based learning rated highest. All HCC domains were also observed at high levels (overall M = 3.76), with collaboration strongest and creativity weakest. A significant positive relationship was established between overall SCL utilization and HCC manifestation (rs = 0.410, p < .001). Differentiated instruction showed the strongest correlation with overall HCC, and active learning was the most broadly associated strategy across all five competency domains. Teacher profile variables, specifically years of teaching experience in Cambodia and participation in professional training, were significantly associated with SCL implementation. The study concludes that while international schools in Phnom Penh consistently apply student-centered approaches, creativity-focused strategies remain underutilized. A six-week capacity-building program was proposed to enhance teacher practice and support the integration of SCL strategies and HCC development in classroom instruction.

papers.title: Game-based learning for health literacy: Lessons from who's Immune Patrol
papers.abstract: Educational approaches that foster early health literacy and trust in health systems are essential for long-term public health resilience. In line with the World Health Organization's (WHO) commitment to increase health literacy in its Second European Programme of Work 2026-2030 and the Sustainable Development Goals 3 and 4, the WHO Regional Office for Europe developed and is helping countries roll out Immune Patrol - a digital, game-based education package designed for schoolchildren aged 10-12 years to improve understanding of the immune system, disease prevention, vaccines and critical thinking. Developed in close collaboration with academic partners and educators, it integrates curriculum-aligned lessons, critical thinking activities, and teacher support materials, available both online and offline. This paper presents Immune Patrol as a case study of an innovative learning approach implemented and evaluated across multiple countries, including Armenia, Georgia and the Republic of Moldova, complemented by new evaluations from Belgium. Evidence from pilot and national rollouts indicates that the game enhances children's knowledge, self-confidence and engagement while supporting teachers in communicating complex health topics in an accessible and non-coercive way. By promoting active learning and positive associations with health information, Immune Patrol contributes to strengthening health literacy and can serve as a model for integrating behavioural and educational approaches into public health promotion. The scalability and adaptability of the model suggest wider potential for application across other health-related topics and educational settings.

papers.title: Shaping meaningful conceptualisations in undergraduate Physical Chemistry using a flipped learning approach
papers.abstract: Physical chemistry is frequently perceived by undergraduate students as conceptually challenging due to its abstract nature and strong reliance on mathematical reasoning. Successful learning requires students to integrate multiple microconcepts and make meaningful connections between macroscopic, microscopic, and symbolic representations. For first‑year students in particular, these demands often result in cognitive overload, low engagement, and limited participation in traditional lecture settings. Flipped learning offers a potential solution to these challenges by reallocating foundational content delivery outside scheduled contact hours and using in‑class time for active learning. While flipped learning has been implemented previously within chemistry education, its application in physical chemistry remains underexplored. The aim of this project is to measure the impact of using bite‑sized pre‑lecture videos on the student engagement and understanding physical chemistry topics during lecture. These videos were co‑created and prepared by student, positioning them as active contributors to curriculum design (student-as-partners approach). These videos focused on core physical chemistry concepts and were provided prior to taught sessions. Two formats-interactive and non‑interactive were developed to compare engagement and perceived understanding. The impact of this approach was evaluated using pre‑ and post‑engagement surveys measuring students’ perceived understanding of the video content. Findings indicate a positive influence of student‑prepared flipped resources on engagement and learning with good student-feedback. The study demonstrates that student‑partnered content creation within a flipped physical chemistry curriculum can meaningfully enhance learning experiences and outcomes.

papers.title: DESIGNING AN INTERACTIVE E-LEARNING LESSON TO SUPPORT GRADE 4 SCIENCE TEACHING: A CASE OF THE TOPIC “FUNGI”
papers.abstract: Digital learning resources are increasingly used in primary education, yet many digital lessons remain primarily presentation-oriented rather than pedagogically structured to support students’ active learning. This study aimed to design and evaluate an interactive E-learning lesson to support Grade 4 Science teaching, using the topic “Fungi” as a case. The lesson was developed through a pedagogical design procedure that included identifying learning outcomes, developing a pedagogical script, preparing multimedia resources, digitizing learning materials, integrating quizzes and interactive activities, and revising the lesson after trial use. A classroom-based quasiexperimental design was employed with one experimental group and one control group, each consisting of 47 Grade 4 students. Data were collected from baseline achievement scores, post-test scores, classroom observation, and student feedback. The results showed that the two groups were comparable at baseline, while the experimental group achieved a higher post-test mean score than the control group (7.91 versus 6.49) and a higher mean gain score (1.72 versus 0.43). Classroom observation and student feedback also indicated that videos, interactive questions, learning games, and immediate feedback supported students’ attention, participation, and perceived understanding. These findings provide preliminary evidence that a pedagogically designed interactive E-learning lesson can support Grade 4 students’ learning outcomes in Science. Further studies with larger samples, longer intervention periods, and more diverse topics are needed to validate and extend these findings.

papers.title: Fortalecimiento de la gobernanza universitaria mediante el desarrollo de competencias comunicativas en inglés en directivos académicos: un estudio aplicado en una institución de educación superior colombiana
papers.abstract: The internationalization of higher education has become one of the main challenges facing universities in the context of globalization, digital transformation, and the continuous expansion of scientific knowledge. Within this framework, strengthening university governance requires academic leaders who possess communication skills that facilitate decision-making, international cooperation, and participation in global academic networks. While bilingual education policies have traditionally focused on students and faculty members, limited research has examined the development of English communication skills among academic leaders and their contribution to institutional governance. This study analyzes the implementation of an English language training program designed for academic administrators at a Colombian higher education institution accredited for high-quality standards. The program was developed under the English for Specific Purposes (ESP) approach and incorporated active learning methodologies, continuous assessment, and professional tasks directly related to university management. Language proficiency was assessed using international standards aligned with the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and the IELTS Academic examination. Results indicate that all participants achieved proficiency levels ranging from B2 to C1 according to the CEFR. Significant improvements were observed in listening, reading, writing, and speaking skills, together with increased confidence in academic communication and participation in international institutional activities. The findings suggest that strengthening English communication skills among academic leaders contributes to enhancing institutional capacities associated with university governance by supporting international cooperation, access to scientific knowledge, academic networking, and the implementation of internationalization strategies within higher education institutions.

papers.title: The Role of Movement and Song Methods on the Development of Gross Motor Skills in Children at TK Negeri 2 Tanah Pinoh
papers.abstract: Gross motor development is a fundamental aspect of early childhood development that supports children's physical, cognitive, social, and emotional growth. However, opportunities for structured physical movement in early childhood education settings are often limited, resulting in insufficient stimulation of children's gross motor skills. This study aimed to analyze the role of the movement and song method in the development of gross motor skills among children at TK Negeri 2 Tanah Pinoh, Melawi Regency, West Kalimantan. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving classroom teachers and Group B children as research participants. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentation and were analyzed using the interactive model of data analysis, including data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings revealed that the movement and song method contributed significantly to the development of children's locomotor, non-locomotor, and manipulative skills. Through activities involving coordinated body movements and rhythmic songs, children demonstrated improved balance, coordination, agility, and body control. In addition, the method increased children's participation, enthusiasm, concentration, and confidence during learning activities. The findings further indicate that movement and song activities create a holistic learning environment that simultaneously supports physical, emotional, and social development. The study concludes that the movement and song method is an effective and developmentally appropriate pedagogical strategy for enhancing gross motor development in early childhood education. Therefore, integrating movement-based learning activities into daily classroom instruction is recommended to promote active learning and support children's overall developmental outcomes.

papers.title: The Effect of Metacognition and Digital Literacy on Listening Skills in the Context of Foreign Language Learning
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the development of listening skills in a foreign-language context through the variables of metacognitive awareness and digital literacy. Listening is not a passive process limited to perceiving auditory input; rather, it is an active learning domain involving multi-layered cognitive operations such as lower-level linguistic decoding and higher-level meaning construction, inferencing, and maintaining discourse coherence. In this regard, how learners plan, monitor, and evaluate their listening processes constitutes a central determinant of listening success. The study was designed as a qualitative inquiry based on a descriptive review model and conducted using document analysis. National and international academic studies were systematically examined, and themes related to metacognitive strategies in listening, components of digital literacy, and the effects of digital listening environments on learning processes were analyzed through thematic analysis. The review results indicate that metacognitive awareness significantly supports listening skill development through planning, monitoring, and evaluation strategies that regulate the listening process. Findings further demonstrate that digital literacy plays a decisive role in the effective use of digital listening materials and strengthens the applicability of metacognitive strategies. Podcasts, online videos, and multimedia-supported listening content provide learners with process control; however, the efficient use of these opportunities appears closely related to learners’ levels of digital literacy and metacognitive awareness. Overall, the study highlights the pedagogical importance of integrating metacognitive strategy instruction and digital literacy-based approaches holistically in developing listening skills and provides a theoretical foundation for future empirical research.

papers.title: Quadriceps Coxae-Sparing Modified Posterior Approach to the Hip Joint for Hemiarthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background: Various approaches have been described for hip arthroplasty 1–3 . The posterior approach to the hip remains a popular choice for hemiarthroplasty 1 . In the classic description, it involves detachment of the short external rotators, which include the quadriceps coxae (QC) (i.e., piriformis, superior gemellus, obturator internus, and inferior gemellus) along with the obturator externus and quadratus femoris ( as needed ) . Since the QC are important for joint stability, detachment during the approach is associated with higher rates of postoperative dislocations 4 , even following subsequent surgical repair of the QC. In the study by Stähelin et al. 5 , 15 of 20 repairs involving the QC had failed by 3 months postoperatively, primarily because the repair site could not withstand the forces of normal weight-bearing during the healing phase. Various muscle-sparing modifications of the conventional approach have been described to reduce the propensity for prosthetic dislocation 6–9 . Hanly et al. 9 described the SPAIRE (Sparing Piriformis and Internus, Repair Externus) technique. This minimally invasive modified posterior approach enables the preservation of the QC, possibly representing the greatest extent of muscle and tendon preservation. The advantages of this QC-sparing technique have been demonstrated in clinical studies of hemiarthroplasty 10,11 and total hip arthroplasty 12 . Description: The patient is anesthetized and placed in a lateral decubitus position. Bolsters are utilized over the pubis and sacral areas to provide stable pelvic orientation. The contralateral limb is flexed at the hip (∼45°) and knee (90°), with adequate padding under the fibular head and lateral malleolus. Another padded bolster is placed between the legs to keep the topmost lower limb in neutral to slight abduction at the hip. The operative limb is flexed at the hip (∼30°), and a 10 to 15-cm straight skin incision is marked on the lateral aspect of hip, centered on the posterolateral tip of the greater trochanter. The deep fascia is opened distally to proximally, incised distally with scissors, and separated proximally with finger dissection. This step creates an intermuscular plane between the gluteus maximus posteriorly and tensor fasciae latae anteriorly. A Charnley hip retractor is applied. Internal rotation of the hip allows identification of the posterior border of the gluteus medius and short external rotators. The fat pad over the QC is swept medially with an abdominal sponge to identify the muscles. A plane is identified between the quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus. Next, a plane is developed between the QC and posterior hip capsule with use of a blunt hemostat from inferior to superior. Abduction of the hip just beyond neutral relaxes the QC and allows superior retraction. The quadratus femoris is detached from the trochanteric crest with use of a diathermy needle until the lesser trochanter is visualized. A capsulotomy is performed in a lazy L-shaped manner, with the first limb of the incision along the distal margin of the QC and the second along the base of the femoral neck. The second limb of the incision raises the musculocapsular flap consisting of the obturator externus along the osseous margin with use of a diathermy needle. This musculocapsular flap is tagged with sutures, which helps in its retraction posteriorly to protect the sciatic nerve and later aids in repair. Bipolar hemiarthroplasty is performed in a conventional manner. The musculocapsular flap is repaired transosseously, and the wound is closed in a layered fashion. Alternatives: Alternatives to this QC-sparing technique include the use of a conventional posterior approach, piriformis-preserving posterior approach, direct lateral approach, modified lateral approach, or direct anterior approach. Rationale: Preservation of the QC helps improve prosthetic hip stability in internal rotation, possibly because of the preserved proprioception. A minimally invasive approach reduces recovery time during rehabilitation. Preservation of the QC does not hinder visualization or result in component malposition 12 . Expected Outcomes: Ball et al. 10 compared the use of a modified muscle-sparing posterior approach versus a standard lateral approach. The authors reported comparable Oxford Hip Scores at 120 days (p = 0.25). Patient function and mobility were similar at 3 days and 120 days, regardless of the surgical approach. Length of hospital stay and return to pre-fracture place of residence were similar. Mortality rates and quality of life were also similar at 120 days postoperatively. Patients who underwent the modified muscle-sparing posterior approach experienced less pain during the early postoperative period. The mean score on the numeric pain rating scale was 4.4 (standard deviation, 2.8) among patients who underwent the modified muscle-sparing posterior approach versus 5.4 (standard deviation, 3.0) among patients who underwent the standard lateral approach (p = 0.04). Important Tips: Place a padded bolster between the legs to keep the topmost lower limb in neutral to slight abduction at the hip. Develop a plane between the QC and posterior hip capsule with use of a blunt hemostat or a Cobb elevator from inferior to superior in order to help mobilize the QC and release their capsular attachments. Hip abduction just beyond neutral relaxes the QC and allows insertion of a Hohmann retractor deep to the QC in order to protect and lever them superiorly. A small Langenbeck retractor inserted deep to the QC protects them from shredding during broaching. Internal rotation at the hip beyond 90° (in 90° flexion and neutral adduction/abduction) further protects the QC from harm.

papers.title: Finite Control Set MPC for DFIG Direct Power Control in Distorted Grids
papers.abstract: This work proposes Finite Control Set - Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) for direct power control of grid-connected Doubly-Fed Induction Generators (DFIG) under distorted voltage situations. The FCS-MPC for DFIG Direct Power Control (DPC) employs the discrete system model, treating active and reactive power as state variables and the rotor voltage vector as input, while minimizing a cost function that reflects the discrepancy between predictions and references. The suggested methodology integrates the Decoupled Double Synchronous Reference Frame Phase-Locked Loop (DDSRF-PLL), facilitating accurate synchronization with the grid, even under distorted voltage conditions, and enhancing the selection of voltage vectors utilized for the rotor. Experimental tests were conducted on a laboratory setup composed of a 3 kW/220 V DFIG, a dSPACE MicroLabBox II platform, a 1 kVA back-to-back converter, and a DC motor used to emulate wind torque. The obtained results demonstrate that the proposed FCS–DPC strategy integrated with the DDSRF–PLL outperforms not only the conventional Deadbeat DPC approach but also the FCS–MPC DPC method reported in [1], particularly under distorted grid-voltage conditions. The proposed method achieves the fastest settling time (0.5 ms), compared to 5.7 ms (Deadbeat) and 5.5 ms [1], and the lowest overshoot (12.2% vs. 31.1% and 33.1%). It also provides superior harmonic performance, with a THD of 4.92% (against 10.13% and 12.82%), the lowest ISE (26.77 dB), and reduced ripple (5.49%). Although the Deadbeat controller presents a slightly smaller steady-state error (0.19%), the proposed strategy maintains a low value (0.94%) while ensuring significantly better transient and harmonic performance. It considerably enhances the literature by filling the gap in research about the performance of conventional FCS-MPC in grid-connected wind generation systems utilizing DFIG.

papers.title: Adaptive Action Representation Learning for Anthropomorphic Grasping
papers.abstract: Anthropomorphic robotic hands offer the potential for human-level dexterity, but their high-dimensional and redundant action spaces pose significant challenges for learning control policies. While recent grasping approaches often reduce the task to static pose prediction followed by motion planning, such methods overlook the dynamic nature of grasping, comprising approach, closure, and lifting phases, each governed by complex contact and inertial dynamics. In contrast, we propose a reinforcement learning framework that learns the entire grasping process by leveraging a synergistic action sub-space. Our method jointly optimizes a control policy and a task-driven action representation via an inverse world model, which learns a low-dimensional latent action space informed by observed state transitions. We evaluate our framework on a subset of YCB objects and show it outperforms baseline methods in success rate and robustness, while also achieving improved zero-shot generalization to unseen objects.

papers.abstract: Manual endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is technically demanding, and existing single-segment robotic tools offer limited dexterity. These limitations motivate the development of more advanced solutions. To address this, decoupled endoscopic submucosal dissection robot (DESectBot), a novel dual-segment continuum robot with a decoupled structure and integrated surgical forceps, enabling six degrees of freedom tip dexterity for improved lesion targeting in ESD, was developed in this work. Deep learning controllers based on gated recurrent units (GRUs) for simultaneous tip position and orientation control, effectively handling the nonlinear coupling between continuum segments, were proposed. The GRU controller was benchmarked against Jacobian-based inverse kinematics, model predictive control (MPC), a feedforward neural network, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network. In addition, a systematic ablation study under identical training conditions showed that, for the considered control task, the GRU achieves better generalization, faster convergence, and higher computational efficiency than the LSTM. In nested-rectangle and Lissajous trajectory tracking tasks, the GRU achieved the lowest position/orientation root-mean-square errors (RMSEs): 1.11 mm/ 4.62$^{\circ }$and 0.81 mm/ 2.59$^{\circ }$, respectively. For orientation control at a fixed position (four target poses), the GRU attained a mean RMSE of 0.14 mm and 0.72$^{\circ }$, outperforming all alternatives. In a peg transfer task, the GRU achieved a 100% success rate (120 success/120 attempts) with an average transfer time of 11.8 s, the standard deviation significantly outperforms no vice-controlled systems. In addition, an ex vivo ESD demonstration—grasping, elevating, and resecting tissue as the scalpel completed the cut—confirmed that DESectBot provides sufficient stiffness to divide thick gastric mucosa and an operative workspace adequate for large lesions. These results confirm that GRU-based control significantly enhances precision, reliability, and usability in ESD surgical training scenarios.

papers.title: Intelligent control algorithm for clean heating temperature based on optical fiber grating temperature sensors
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent control algorithm based on fiber Bragg grating temperature sensors to address the problems of inaccurate temperature measurement caused by electromagnetic interference in traditional temperature sensors in geothermal clean heating systems, poor adaptability of conventional PID controllers to complex and variable working conditions, and large control overshoot. This algorithm uses fiber Bragg grating sensors to construct a time-division multiplexing sensing network, which utilizes its anti-electromagnetic interference characteristics and the linear relationship between temperature and wavelength to solve the problem of accurate temperature measurement in complex geothermal heating environments, providing real-time and reliable data for temperature control. In terms of control indicators, time squared multiplied by absolute error integral is used instead of traditional absolute error integral to adapt to conditions with variable parameters. At the same time, the back propagation neural network is introduced to perform online adaptive tuning of the proportional, integral, and derivative parameters of the PID controller, enabling the controller to automatically adjust control parameters based on the real-time operating status of the system, and improve its response capability to complex working conditions such as sudden changes in thermal load and outdoor temperature. The experimental results show that under high interference levels, the sensor network can still stably transmit 20 data packets within 100 s. Compared with existing methods based on wireless temperature sensors, thermocouple sensors, and model predictive control, the control overshoot of this algorithm is reduced to 8%, and the adjustment time is shortened to 10.2 min. During the 24-h continuous operation test, when the outdoor temperature fluctuated within the range of 5–12 °C, the indoor temperature remained stable at around 25 °C without any noticeable fluctuations. This algorithm provides a temperature control scheme for geothermal clean heating with anti-interference ability, adaptive adjustment ability, and high-precision control performance.

papers.title: Hybrid Multi‐Agent Reinforcement Learning and Consensus Control for Dynamic V2G‐Enabled Voltage Regulation in Active Distribution Networks
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Active low‐voltage distribution networks with high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and vehicle‐to‐grid (V2G)‐enabled electric vehicles (EVs) face significant voltage regulation challenges due to renewable intermittency, stochastic EV behaviour, and dynamic plug‐and‐play participation of mobile storage resources. Conventional voltage‐control approaches are often reactive, model‐dependent, or unable to accommodate time‐varying agent populations in real time. This paper proposes a Hybrid Multi‐Agent Reinforcement Learning and Consensus (HMC) framework for decentralised voltage regulation in PV‐rich active distribution networks. The proposed architecture integrates three coordinated layers: (i) fast local droop control for immediate stabilisation, (ii) multi‐agent proximal policy optimisation (MAPPO) under centralised training and decentralised execution (CTDE) for anticipatory decision‐making, and (iii) a modified ratio‐consensus mechanism with dynamic graph management for fair coordination and seamless real‐time integration of transient V2G resources. The control problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) considering stochastic PV/load variations and EV user constraints. The proposed framework is validated on a modified IEEE 33‐bus distribution feeder using realistic stochastic datasets and compared with distributed consensus control (DCC), model predictive control (MPC), alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and standalone deep reinforcement learning baselines. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces voltage violations by up to 82.9%, decreases network losses by 18.0%, and lowers BESS cycling by 36.8% while maintaining 94.7% EV user satisfaction. Furthermore, the framework remains robust under forecast uncertainty and communication impairments, including ±30% forecast errors, 500 ms communication delays, and 20% packet loss, demonstrating its practical suitability for future V2G‐enabled active distribution networks.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Dual-Rate Predictive Control With ELM-Based Learning and Kalman State Estimation
papers.abstract: Despite extensive advances in nonlinear model predictive control and learning-based system identification, robust control of nonlinear systems under asynchronous sensing, model uncertainty, and measurement noise remains fundamentally challenging. In particular, conventional MPC frameworks rely on accurate affine or locally linearized models and single-rate measurements, which limits their applicability to practical systems exhibiting strong nonlinearities, dual-rate sensing, and time-varying dynamics. This limitation prevents many real-world cyber–physical systems from fully benefiting from MPC’s robustness and constraint-handling capabilities. This work addresses this long-standing challenge by proposing a unified dual-rate adaptive control framework that integrates online learning, state estimation, and constrained predictive control for nonlinear systems. Unlike existing learning-based MPC approaches that require offline training, fixed model structures, or heuristic gain tuning, the proposed method provides adaptive modeling and control entirely online without prior system knowledge. This work introduces three main contributions: (1) a dual-rate unscented Kalman filter capable of reliable state estimation under asynchronous and sparse measurements, (2) an online extreme learning machine–based NARX modeling framework embedded directly within the MPC prediction model, and (3) a Lyapunov-based adaptive control architecture ensuring practical closed-loop stability and robustness. The learned model is continuously updated in real time and used within a constrained nonlinear MPC formulation with adaptive steady-state target computation, enabling accurate trajectory tracking under parametric uncertainties, external disturbances, and measurement noise. Simulation results under multiple challenging scenarios demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves superior tracking performance and robustness compared to conventional PID schemes, highlighting its effectiveness for high-precision digital control of nonlinear systems.

papers.title: Wind Turbine Load Reduction Predictive Control Strategy Based on Dynamic Model and Data‐Driven Approach
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To suppress the aerodynamic and structural loads of large‐scale wind turbines and mitigate modelling errors induced by parameter uncertainties and unmodeled dynamics, this paper proposes a data‐driven corrected dynamic modelling and predictive control strategy for wind turbines operating within a full operational wind speed range of 3–25 m/s. A hybrid modelling framework is established by combining a physics‐based dynamic model with a three‐layer neural network correction module. Specifically, full wind‐speed‐range operational data collected from Bladed simulations are employed to refine the key parameters of the mechanism model and the neural network with a 64‐32‐5 neuron configuration and dual sigmoid/linear activation functions are adopted to compensate for residual dynamic errors, effectively improving the model accuracy under time‐varying wind conditions. On this basis, a data‐driven dynamic model predictive control (DDMPC) strategy is developed for wind turbine load reduction. Meanwhile, a polynomial wind speed prediction model is constructed to fuse Lidar‐measured and power‐estimated wind speed data, so as to improve the wind preview performance of the control system. Simulations are carried out on a 6.25 MW wind turbine covering the entire 3–25 m/s wind speed range. The results show that compared with conventional physics‐based MPC and PID control, the proposed DDMPC reduces the Y‐direction tower‐base bending moment by 13.8% and the Y‐direction blade‐root bending moment by 5.8%. Further field tests on a practical 10 MW wind turbine demonstrate that the DDMPC strategy significantly improves the stability of generator speed and output power under medium‐low and medium‐high wind speed conditions. This work provides an effective technical solution for high‐precision dynamic modelling and load‐optimal control of large‐scale wind turbines, offering promising engineering application value for improving wind turbine structural safety and operational stability.

papers.title: Parametric Optimization of DC–DC Boost Converter Using LSTM–HHO for Renewable Energy Systems Under Bounded Time‐Varying Loads
papers.abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic (PV) and fuel cell systems demands highly efficient and adaptive DC–DC power conversion. However, existing DC–DC boost converters face several challenges, such as poor adaptability to time‐varying loads, inefficient parameter tuning, and increased switching stress during fluctuating operating conditions. Traditional control strategies including, proportional‐integral (PI) controllers and basic neural networks, are unable to maintain performance under dynamic conditions. This paper presents a long short‐term memory and Harris Hawks optimization (LSTM–HHO) framework for parametric optimization of DC–DC boost converter architectures. A detailed mathematical model of the boost converter under time‐varying load conditions is developed, aiming to describe the key problems and their theoretical solutions. The model uses LSTM networks to predict time‐varying load behaviors and adjusts control parameters through the HHO algorithm. The framework is validated across multiple converter topologies, including conventional boost, flyback, and interleaved configurations, using advanced semiconductor devices such as Silicon Carbide metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistor (SiC‐MOSFET) and Gallium Nitride high‐electron‐mobility transistor (GaN‐HEMT). Simulation results under bounded time‐varying load conditions and source perturbation scenarios show that the proposed framework achieves improved voltage regulation, reduced output ripple, lower switching stress, and faster convergence than conventional PI, fuzzy‐logic, deep reinforcement learning‐enhanced model predictive control (DRL–MPC), and RBF‐FLC approaches. Validation with nonideal simulations and hardware‐in‐the‐loop (HIL)/controller‐in‐the‐loop (CIL) testing under bounded time‐varying loads R ( t ) ∈ [ R min , R max ] confirms reduced ripple and switch stress at embedded‐feasible compute cost.

papers.title: PhyP-Net: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning for Sub-Second EV Power Demand Prediction in Hybrid Energy Storage Systems
papers.abstract: Hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) combining batteries and supercapacitors require sub-second power demand forecasts for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) in electric vehicles (EVs). However, existing EV power prediction studies operate at temporal resolutions of one second or coarser, leaving the sub-second regime unexplored. This paper proposes PhyP-Net, a physics-constrained power forecasting network that predicts EV power demand at 10 Hz resolution—matching the NMPC control cycle—using 11 input features derived from 7 controller area network (CAN) bus signals. The architecture integrates a residual long short-term memory (LSTM) encoder with attention-based temporal pooling and a multi-head predictor that decomposes the 50-step (5 s) horizon into short-, mid-, and long-term heads. Training combines a time-weighted data-driven loss with a Huber-based physics constraint enforcing the powertrain relationship and multi-task learning of torque and revolutions per minute (RPM) auxiliary targets. Experiments on a Tesla Model 3 dataset show that PhyP-Net attains a short-term coefficient of determination of 88.90% and the strongest 5 s multi-step accuracy. Although a linear baseline achieves a lower one-step peak failure rate (PFR), PhyP-Net provides the most robust transient tracking across the full horizon and substantially outperforms the recurrent and Transformer baselines, achieving the best overall accuracy–reliability balance. Ablation shows that multi-task learning produces the largest impact on transient reliability (PFR), whereas removing the physics constraint increases the internal-consistency violation by 58% at negligible statistical cost. Embedded inference on an NVIDIA Jetson consumes 4.64 ms per sample (4.6% of the real-time budget), confirming real-time inference feasibility on embedded hardware.

papers.title: Flexible Power Supply and Distribution Based on FDN for Photovoltaic Tobacco Logistics Warehouses
papers.abstract: Industrial plants should implement sophisticated renewable-energy-based distribution systems to guarantee a continuous and reliable power supply and enhanced operational efficiency under varying loading conditions. A Flexible Power Supply and Distribution System (FPSDS) utilize the concept of Flexible Distribution Networks (FDN) for photovoltaic-contracted tobacco warehouse facilities. The integrated power system connects PV panels to a multi-port bidirectional DC-DC converter, which operates with a BESS and a full-bridge PWM inverter to provide bi-directional energy management and increased power reliability. The system achieves enhancement by integrating three control mechanisms, which include DLD for real-time energy distribution, IPR for loss minimization and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) for adaptive system optimisation. The system manages dynamic voltage and power regimes and current movements through predictive behaviour prediction, which utilizes Model Predictive Control (MPC). Simulation results demonstrate enhanced electric power management that leads to better voltage systems alongside lower transmission losses and superior peak demand control. Such a solution enables both real-time capabilities and scalability benefits while enhancing operational durability and suits warehouses with energetic systems that function dynamically. The research creates a smart solution to incorporate renewable power sources within logistics operations that builds sustainable energy frameworks for decentralizing power systems. The proposed system introduces an integrated control framework combining Dynamic Load Distribution, Intelligent Power Routing, and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning within an FDN for photovoltaic-integrated warehouses. The approach demonstrates a 15–20% reduction in transmission losses, a 12–18% increase in overall energy efficiency, and improved voltage stability by maintaining deviations within 5%. These results confirm the novelty of this research in achieving adaptive, intelligent, and scalable power distribution for logistics facilities.

papers.title: A Novel Predictive Control Approach Based on Hybrid Deep Learning Algorithm for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting in Microgrid
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) installations and their inherent intermittency due to weather variability, advanced energy control strategies have become essential for modern microgrid operation. In this context, reliable short‐term forecasting and optimal decision‐making are critical to ensure stable and efficient energy management. This work proposes a predictive energy management framework based on a parallel deep learning architecture combining long short‐term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, whose hyperparameters are optimized using a multiobjective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm for accurate PV power forecasting. The developed forecasting model is explicitly integrated into a model predictive control (MPC) scheme for real‐time microgrid energy management. In this MPC framework, the LSTM–GRU–MOPSO model provides multi‐step‐ahead PV power predictions that serve as key inputs to the optimization problem solved at each control interval (5 min). The MPC then determines optimal power dispatch decisions, including energy storage charging/discharging and grid interaction, while respecting system constraints and minimizing operational cost and power imbalance. The proposed approach is validated using a real PV dataset collected in Maroua, Far North Cameroon, under daily, weekly, and monthly prediction horizons. Results demonstrate that the hybrid forecasting model achieves high accuracy across daily, weekly, and monthly horizons, with R 2 values of 0.9984, 0.9988, and 0.9934, and RMSE values of 0.2096, 0.2034, and 0.3501, respectively. Comparative analysis shows that the proposed LSTM–GRU–MOPSO model outperforms conventional methods such as LSTM, GRU, support vector machine (SVM), and feedforward neural networks (FFNN), as well as hybrid architectures including LSTM–CNN and LSTM–RNN. The integration with MPC further enhances system reliability by enabling predictive, constraint‐aware, and adaptive microgrid energy management.
papers.venue: Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering

papers.title: Comparative Study on High-Precision Artificial Neural Network Fitting Methods for NMPC under MPPT Operating Conditions of Wind Turbines
papers.abstract: Up to now, there remain difficulties in modeling large-scale engineering equipment with complex nonlinear characteristics, especially for the large-scale wind turbines. Based on the powerful learning capability of neural networks, this study adopts an approximation method with fast response characteristics to fit the output results of nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). First, based on the dynamic characteristics of maximum wind energy extraction (MWEE) of wind turbines, a constrained NMPC rolling optimization prediction model is established, and a dataset of torque control laws with prediction horizons of 5, 6, and 7 steps respectively is generated. Second, the fitting performance of two feedforward networks, namely the artificial neural network (ANN) and feedforward neural network (FFNN), is compared and analyzed, and the positive correlation between the prediction horizon and fitting accuracy is clarified. Finally, three types of temporal neural networks, including the one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and temporal convolutional network (TCN), are introduced, and a comprehensive evaluation of fitting accuracy, convergence characteristics and robustness is conducted based on five quantitative metrics including mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE). The results show that: feedforward networks can achieve effective approximation of the nonlinear control law of NMPC; temporal neural networks can significantly break through the performance limitations of static networks, and the coefficient of determination (R2) of all three temporal networks is greater than 0.99, which fully meets the accuracy requirements of industrial control. This study verifies the feasibility of replacing the online solution of NMPC with a data-driven neural network fitting method, clarifies the differentiated engineering application scenarios of different network architectures, and provides a theoretical basis and technical solution for the high-performance real-time control of wind turbines under maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operating conditions.

papers.title: Strategies Based Control and Modeling Grid - Connected Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems with Power Electronic Interface Integration
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study based on the smart intelligence technique used for modeling and control of a grid-connected solar PV systems by dynamically utilizing a power electronic interface. The integration of solar PV systems with the electrical grid necessitates advanced control strategies to govern efficient and operate reliably. It focuses on the development of a detailed mathematical model of the PV system, encompassing the PV array, DC-DC converter, inverter and grid interface. The PV array is designed particularly on the single-diode equivalent circuit, allowing for accurate representation of its I-V characteristics under varying environmental conditions. The DC-DC converter, typically a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller, is vital for optimizing the power output that comes from the PV array. Various MPPT methods are assed, with Perturb & Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (IC) methods being extensively analyzed for their performance and efficiency. The inverter is a critical component that are used in converting the DC power from the PV array to AC power adaptable with the grid. This study explores different inverter topologies and control strategies, including Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) techniques and grid synchronization techniques. The control system ensures that the inverter output is synchronized with the grid voltage and frequency, needed for maintaining the power quality and power stability. Furthermore, the paper discusses about implementation of grid for well support need for smooth functions like reactive power compensation, voltage regulation and fault ride-through capabilities. Advanced control algorithms, including Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers, Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) based methods are examined for their potential to enhance system performance. Simulation results are presented to validate the proposed models and control strategies, demonstrating their effectiveness in achieving optimal power transfer, maintaining grid stability and follows with grid codes. The research highlights the importance that reflect the robust control mechanisms that ensure the seamless integration of solar PV systems into the existing power grid infrastructure.

papers.title: Event-Triggered Hierarchical DDPG-MPC for Dynamic High-Point Tracking of Mobile Platforms on Unstructured Terrain
papers.abstract: The challenge of ensuring dynamic stability for mobile platforms on rough terrain is a key issue in robotics. Traditional stabilization methods involve frequent center-of-gravity adjustments, leading to increased energy consumption and mechanical wear. These methods are limited to one-dimensional adjustments and struggle to adapt to diverse terrains. To overcome these challenges, we propose an Event-Triggered Hierarchical Control Framework (ET-DDPG-MPC) for stabilizing mobile platforms following circular paths. This framework divides prediction and execution: a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) agent forecasts acceleration disturbances using historical data, while an Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control with Dynamic Stability Segmentation (DSS-MPC) replaces continuous tracking. This separation combines the DDPG agent's predictive abilities with the precise execution of MPC to reduce unnecessary actions and enhance adaptability on complex terrains. The controller identifies stable time windows in platform attitude, issuing optimal slider-movement commands during window transitions or significant target point drift to maintain stability. This control approach, combining computational continuity with physical discontinuity, minimizes adjustments to conserve attitude within stable windows, reducing energy consumption and execution frequency. An extended observation space considering recent platform dynamics and a composite reward enhancing smooth, precise tracking addresses training challenges for reinforcement-learning agents in dynamic environments. Simulations using a comprehensive toolchain (PyTorch, CasADi, IPOPT, and custom terrain modules) show that the ET-DDPG-MPC framework outperforms continuous-tracking MPC and PPO-based methods in stability, accuracy, and robustness. Frequency-domain analysis further validates these results. In extreme-gradient tests, our framework achieves a maximum slope ratio 375% higher than baseline methods (MPC: 8°, PPO-MPC: 35°, ours: 38°) while maintaining an average tracking deviation within 0.1°, showcasing its exceptional performance and practical applicability in complex dynamic scenarios.

papers.title: Modular Energy Management via Distributed and Predictive Optimization for Fuel Cell-Battery Shipboard Microgrids
papers.abstract: Electrification of ship power systems plays a central role in the mobility transition toward sustainable transportation. The integration of a large number of components with distinct characteristics into a shipboard microgrid benefits from a modular design and standardized interfaces. Key challenges lie in the variety of component characteristics, and an evolution of parameters during the power system operation. Further, topology alterations can occur over time, requiring a reformulation of the optimal power dispatch problem. Accordingly, a modular energy management strategy must be adaptive to these changes. This work explores a distributed energy management architecture with a central coordinating agent, realized via Lagrangian dual decomposition and a gradient-based solver. This architecture ensures both local feasibility while reaching global optimality and a power balance through a consensus mechanism. Parameter changes are incorporated in local cost functions, making extensive data exchange with a central unit obsolete. Handling a variable number of power system components, this approach is resilient to component faults, topology redesigns, and component degradation. The method is applied to a fuel-cell battery hybrid harbor tug equipped with multiple parallel modules with unique ratings and state-of-health. The energy management strategy minimizes total operating costs, based on hydrogen fuel consumption and cell degradation. Extensive mission simulations show similar performance for the distributed approach and a centralized equivalent. The predictive strategy is demonstrably superior to instantaneous optimization, yielding a cost reduction of $18.3 \%$ with a $15 \,{\mathrm{min}}$ prediction horizon. The model predictive control performance increases with the horizon length, reducing operation costs by an additional $6.0 \%$ at $60 \,{\mathrm{min}}$ . In addition, a local decision-making heuristic shows promising potential for the cell degradation via optimized timing of on- and off switching. At $15 \,{\mathrm{min}}$ , this reduces operation costs by $3.0 \%$ and at $60 \,{\mathrm{min}}$ by $12.7 \%$ . Finally, the distributed optimization is deployed on real-time target machines to showcase the applicability of the approach on actual controller and communication hardware.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Augmented Multifeature Fusion Ensemble for Accurate and Uncertain PV Power Forecasting
papers.abstract: This article presents a short-term (1-h ahead) physics-guided multirepresentation feature fusion framework for photovoltaic (PV) power prediction with uncertainty quantification based on quantile regression for interval forecasting. The proposed hybrid methodology integrates feature-representation fusion, deep learning architectures, including long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU), and machine learning models, such as support vector regression (SVR) and random forest (RF), along with dimensionality reduction techniques, namely principal component analysis (PCA) and autoencoder (AE), and a fully defined physics-based digital twin (DT) model with explicit irradiance-to-power equations and parameter calibration. The DT residual, computed causally using only training data, is incorporated as a physics-informed feature to capture unmodeled nonlinearities. PIs are learned using the pinball (quantile) loss function, replacing heuristic assumptions, and feature-representation fusion reduces uncertainty while enhancing robustness. Validation on real meteorological datasets from Izki and Manah stations (2017–2023) shows that conventional feature sets achieve root mean squared error (RMSE) values between 0.14–0.17 with coefficient of determination ( $R^{2}$ ) ranging from 0.47–0.61. Incorporating DT residuals significantly improves performance, while maintaining realistic generalization performance, with LSTM achieving RMSE $\approx$ 0.0105 and $R^{2}$ up to 0.9979. SVR and RF models also benefit, achieving RMSE $\leq 0.0525$ and $R^{2} \geq 0.9467$ . Comprehensive evaluation including ensemble comparisons, ablation studies, and uncertainty metrics, namely prediction interval coverage probability and mean prediction interval width, confirms high coverage and sharpness, while feature-representation fusion ensures consistent, low-uncertainty predictions. Further experiments on a physically inspired synthetic dataset with explicitly defined generation process and temporal resolution of 1000 samples demonstrate similar trends. Using DT residual features, LSTM and GRU achieve $R^{2} > 0.998$ with RMSE $\approx 0.042$ , while RF reaches $R^{2} = 0.897$ and a relatively higher RMSE $\approx 0.326$ . PCA and AE representations improve computational efficiency but provide comparatively lower predictive accuracy. Direct comparison between individual models and the proposed ensemble highlights the robustness and stability of the fusion strategy, particularly in high-noise conditions. In summary, the framework offers a reproducible, physically grounded, and uncertainty-aware solution for next-generation solar energy forecasting, explicitly quantifying prediction uncertainty and leveraging physics-informed residuals to enhance predictive reliability and interpretability across both real and synthetic scenarios.

papers.title: Comparative Time Series Machine Learning Model for Nuclear Reactor Water Plant Coolant System Data at RTP Malaysia
papers.abstract: The secondary cooling system in a nuclear reactor plays a critical role in ensuring operational stability, safety, and performance. Accurate forecasting of key process parameters such as temperature, pressure, and flow rate within this system is essential for early anomaly detection and predictive maintenance. This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of ten time series forecasting models, spanning statistical models such as autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average, exponential smoothing state space model (ETS), and Prophet; machine learning like support vector machine for time series, random forest, and gradient boosted trees; as well as deep learning architectures such as gated recurrent unit (GRU), long short-term memory, and WaveNet, using real-world supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) sensor data from the PUSPATI TRIGA Reactor (RTP) research reactor in Malaysia. The models were trained and evaluated across five essential signals, which are TT003, TT004, PT002, PT003, and FT002, and their performances were benchmarked using multiple metrics, i.e. root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error, R-squared (R2), mean absolute percentage error, residual analysis, uncertainty quantification, anomaly response, and computational feasibility, which is model size, inference, and training time. Results demonstrate that GRU outperforms all other models in accuracy (e.g. RMSE < 0.1), resilience to transient anomalies, and computational efficiency; that is, model size = 0.125 MB, inference time = 77.5 ms/sample, and training time = 70.3 s. WaveNet, while competitive in accuracy, exhibited higher latency and resource demands. Statistical models such as ARIMA and ETS failed to capture nonlinear and abrupt behavior under reactor transients, resulting in poor generalization and negative R2 scores. Residual and uncertainty analysis further confirmed that deep learning models maintain robust prediction quality under dynamic operating conditions. The ability of GRU to adapt to anomalies and provide confidence-aware forecasts highlights its suitability for integration into nuclear SCADA systems. This study is the first to provide an end-to-end comparison of forecasting models, including deep neural architectures, with full-spectrum evaluation for nuclear reactor cooling system data. These findings support the deployment of GRU-based models in safety-critical environments and pave the way for intelligent, real-time, and energy-efficient monitoring frameworks in next-generation nuclear reactor operations.

papers.title: Managing Classroom Dynamics and Students' Performance: A Case of Uganda's Pedagogical Shift
papers.abstract: The management of classroom dynamics has emerged as a critical determinant of student performance within the evolving landscape of Uganda's higher education system. As universities across Uganda transition toward learner-centred pedagogical models propelled by national policy frameworks including the National Council for Higher Education (NCHE) quality standards and the Uganda Vision 2040 human capital agenda. The classroom is increasingly understood not merely as a physical space for instruction but as a complex social ecosystem in which power relations, cultural norms, instructional strategies, and individual learning differences converge to shape academic outcomes. This article critically examines the assessment of teaching through the lens of classroom dynamics management and its documented effects on student performance, drawing on Uganda as a primary case study with comparative reference to the broader East African and sub-Saharan African pedagogical landscape. Grounded in Lev Vygotsky's sociocultural theory, Paolo Freire's critical pedagogy, and contemporary classroom ecology frameworks, the paper interrogates the theoretical and empirical dimensions of classroom management in Ugandan higher education. It analyses structural impediment including overcrowded lecture halls, resource scarcity, linguistic diversity, gender dynamics, and instructor preparation gaps alongside promising pedagogical innovations including active learning methodologies, differentiated instruction, inclusive classroom design, and technology-enhanced engagement. The article further maps the implications of classroom dynamics management for the broader assessment of teaching infrastructure, arguing that student performance outcomes cannot be meaningfully evaluated in abstraction from the classroom environments in which they are produced. Recommendations are advanced for instructor professional development, institutional policy reform, and national quality assurance realignment.

papers.title: The Effect of Teaching Concept Map Drawing on Self-Regulation, Retention, and Comprehension in Sixth-Grade Science
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of teaching concept map drawing on self-regulation, retention, and comprehension of science concepts among sixth-grade female students. This quasi-experimental research employed a pretest-posttest design with a control group. The statistical population included all sixth-grade female students in Marand City during the 2024–2025 academic year. Fifty students were selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to experimental and control groups (25 each). The experimental group received eight sessions of concept map training based on a validated instructional package, while the control group received traditional classroom instruction. Data were collected using the Bouffard Self-Regulation Questionnaire (1995) and teacher-made tests of retention and comprehension. Data analysis was conducted using multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA) via SPSS-27 software. The results indicated that concept map instruction had a significant effect on self-regulation (F=5.505, p=0.023, η²=0.109), retention (F=62.252, p<0.001, η²=0.580), and comprehension (F=50.054, p<0.001, η²=0.640). Students in the experimental group outperformed the control group in all posttest variables. The Wilks’ Lambda test (λ=0.195, F=43.241, p<0.001, η²=0.751) confirmed the overall multivariate effect of concept map training on dependent variables. Teaching through concept map drawing significantly improved students’ self-regulation, retention, and comprehension in science learning. The visual and structural organization of concepts promoted meaningful learning and cognitive engagement. It is recommended that science teachers integrate concept mapping as an active learning strategy to enhance conceptual understanding and self-directed learning.

papers.title: Multi-media as means of instruction
papers.abstract: In order to improve academic achievement and educational engagement, multimedia instruction which incorporates text, audio, video, and interactive elements has become a global standard. By 2025, this style of training will have evolved from basic material delivery to complex ecosystems that use mobile-first microlearning, artificial intelligence (AI), and virtual/augmented reality (AR/VR). Asia with more than 400 million internet users in Southeast Asia alone, the area has adopted digital technology at a rapid “sprint.” School administrators are spearheading a faster digital change in East Asia, but experts warn of a “digital divide” where disenfranchised students lack the skills to fully benefit from. Europe standardized frameworks, like the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu), which coordinates the use of instructional technology throughout the continent to guarantee good pedagogical quality, are what define integration. Australia Global trends indicate that it adopts Western methods of high AR/VR integration and mobile learning to reach remote populations, even though particular 2025 reports for Australia were not included in the sample. Africa with an emphasis on how multimedia might enhance academic performance as demonstrated by recent studies where pupils demonstrated notable improvements in science subjects the African Union is actively working to standardize learning assessments through a new continental framework. North America in order to solve issues like student engagement and administrative efficiency, educational institutions are at the forefront of integrating generative AI and immersive technology into classrooms. South America Multimedia elements, such as interactive video production, are employed in rural areas to increase “active learning competencies” and close the equity gap between urban and rural communities.

papers.title: The trajectory of the Health and Spirituality discipline at a public university in Amazonas: an experience report
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction: The inclusion of spirituality in health professional education has been increasingly recognized as a relevant component for promoting comprehensive care, in line with the biopsychosocial-spiritual model and current scientific evidence. Despite this, its institutionalization within curricula remains limited and heterogeneous. Experience report: This is a descriptive report of the institutional trajectory of the elective course Health and Spirituality at a Public University in Amazonas, continuously offered between 2019 and 2025 to students of Medicine, Nursing, and Dentistry. The course comprises a 30-hour workload, is organized into theoretical and applied units, is grounded in the biopsychosocial-spiritual model, employs active learning methodologies, and adopts a predominantly formative assessment approach. The report describes the implementation process, successive updates to the syllabus, the didactic-pedagogical organization, assessment strategies, and the articulation with academic and scientific activities, including institutional events and the creation of the Amazonas Academic League of Health and Spirituality (LIASE Amazonas). Over 14 semesters, 619 students participated in the course, with consistently high demand for enrollment. Discussion: The experience shows that adopting the biopsychosocial-spiritual model as a pedagogical framework provides a consistent conceptual basis for integrating spirituality into health education, overcoming biomedical reductionism. The didactic-pedagogical organization of the course fostered critical reflection, the development of relational competencies, and an ethical approach to the spiritual dimension of care, in line with national and international recommendations for health education. The articulation between teaching and extension, materialized through integration with LIASE Amazonas, expanded the formative scope of the initiative. Conclusion: The experience demonstrates that the structured inclusion of spirituality in health education is feasible, relevant, and aligned with current educational guidelines, reinforcing the importance of systematizing and disseminating similar experiences to strengthen this field in health education.

papers.title: Innovative Methods in Teaching Law to Non-Law Students: A Proposed Framework for Experiential, Digital and Interdisciplinary Legal Learning
papers.abstract: Teaching law to non-law students appears to be challenging for law lecturers. Non-law students background such as business, accounting, management, entrepreneurship and so on generally require practical legal literacy rather than traditional doctrinal competencies of normal legal students. Conventional lecture-centred approaches may be insufficient for learners who encounter unfamiliar legal terminology, judicial decisions and statutory materials without an established framework for legal reasoning. This conceptual article synthesises scholarship on constructivist, experiential and active learning together with recent work on problem-based learning, simulation, gamification, visualisation, flipped learning, authentic assessment and generative artificial intelligence in legal education. It focuses especially on the needs of non-law learners and on developments relevant to Malaysian and wider Asian higher education. The synthesis indicates that effective innovation requires more than digitising conventional instruction; it requires redesigning learning around professional context, participation, application, source verification and reflection. On that basis, the article proposes the C.L.E.A.R. Legal Learning Framework, comprising Contextualisation, Learning by Experience, Engagement and Collaboration, Application through Technology, and Reflective Legal Literacy. The framework positions legal literacy, rather than reproduction of doctrine, as the principal outcome for non-law students and treats technology as a means rather than an end. It further proposes AI legal-verification exercises in which students evaluate generated legal information against legislation, cases and other authoritative sources. The article concludes that innovative legal pedagogy is most effective when legal principles are connected with students' disciplinary knowledge, future professional decisions and critical digital literacy, while assessment rewards reasoned application rather than recall alone.
